A free GO Wild Area: Gigantamax Machamp Power Up Timed Research is available globally from November 6–8, 2026. Trainers must log in during this weekend to receive the research, but have until November 15 to complete it.

The research rewards a Gigantamax Machamp encounter for exploring 5 km, alongside Machop Candy, Candy XL, Max Particles, Stardust, and other items.

GO Wild Area: Gigantamax Machamp Power Up! Timed Research

Gigantamax Machamp

This Timed Research will award an encounter with Gigantamax Machamp, who can help you take on Gigantamax Duraludon and other powerful Pokémon appearing during Pokémon GO Wild Area: Global.

Task Reward
Explore 5 km Gigantamax Machamp
Catch a Pokémon on 2 different days 110× Machop Candy
Catch a Pokémon on 3 different days 600× Max Particle
Catch a Pokémon on 4 different days 110× Machop Candy XL
Catch a Pokémon on 5 different days 800× Max Particle
Rewards
  • 30,000× Stardust
  • 10× Ultra Ball

Trainers in New Zealand were among the first to report receiving the free Timed Research, confirming that the Gigantamax Machamp encounter is awarded for exploring 5 km.

Note on Timed Research

You must log in between Friday, November 6, at 10:00 a.m. and Sunday, November 8, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. local time to receive this Timed Research. The tasks associated with Timed Research must be completed and their rewards must be claimed before Sunday, November 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. local time.

item.content:encoded:
Mega Clefable debuts during Clefable Super Mega Raid Day on Saturday, November 28, 2026, from 2:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. local time.

Mega Clefable appears in Super Mega Raids with an increased chance to be Shiny, and you can get up to six free Raid Passes from Gyms. Clefable caught from these raids comes with Mega Level 1 already unlocked, and Mega Clefable can now reach the Super Max Mega Level and use Moonblast+. Read on for CP ranges, bonuses, the Global Challenge, the event ticket and the best counters.

Featured Pokémon

Mega Clefable

Mega Clefable debuts in Super Mega Raids during the event. Mega Clefable is a Fairy and Flying type Pokémon.

Clefable caught from raids has the following CP ranges:

  • From 1322 CP to 1392 CP with no weather boost
  • From 1653 CP to 1741 CP with the Cloudy weather boost

Regular and Shiny Comparison

Clefable Clefable

Bonuses

  • Increased chance to encounter Shiny Clefable from Super Mega Raids
  • Up to six free Raid Passes from spinning Gym Photo Discs
  • Clefable caught from Super Mega Raids will have Mega Level 1 unlocked
  • Remote Raid limit increased to 20 from Friday, November 27, at 5:00 p.m. to Saturday, November 28, 2026, at 8:00 p.m. PST

Timed Research

Complete the event Timed Research for a Premium Battle Pass and an encounter with Metagross, one of the best Mega Clefable counters. Claim the rewards before the research expires.

  • Metagross

Event Ticket Bonuses

For US$4.99 (or the equivalent pricing tier in your local currency), you can buy an event ticket with the following bonuses:

  • Up to 14 Raid Passes from spinning Gym Photo Discs
  • Increased chance to get Rare Candy XL from Raid Battles
  • 5,000 extra XP from Super Mega Raids
  • 5,000 extra Stardust from Super Mega Raids

These bonuses are active on Saturday, November 28, 2026, from 2:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. local time.

  • The ticket is sold in the in-game shop until Saturday, November 28, at 5:00 p.m. local time. It can’t be bought with PokéCoins.
  • You can gift tickets to friends you’re at least Great Friends with. Purchases are non-refundable.
  • Better deal: The Clefable Super Mega Raid Day Ultra Ticket Box in the Pokémon GO Web Store costs the same US$4.99 and adds a bonus Premium Battle Pass.

New Mega Level: Super Max

For the first time in Pokémon GO, you can raise Mega Clefable’s Mega Level all the way to Super Max. As revealed during Mega Finale, Pokémon that unlock Super Max can learn an additional Charged Attack while Mega Evolved. Read more in the official Mega Evolution update and more Mega updates posts.

Moonblast+

Mega Clefable can use an additional Charged Attack, Moonblast+:

  • Trainer Battles: 80 power, with a chance to lower the opponent’s Attack by one stage.
  • Raid Battles: 160 power.

The attack gets stronger as Clefable’s Mega Level rises. You must reach the third Mega Level, Max, before you can raise it to Super Max.

Mega Evolving alone won’t get you to Super Max. You’ll also need to spend Clefable Mega Energy to power it up, so join as many Mega Raids as you can.

Global Challenge

Trainers worldwide complete Raid Battles together to unlock as many Global Challenge tiers as possible. The challenge runs from Friday, November 27, at 5:00 p.m. PST to Saturday, November 28, 2026, at 8:00 p.m. PST.

The more tiers completed, the bigger the boosts Mega Clefable gets from Monday, November 30, at 12:00 p.m. PST until Sunday, December 13, at 12:00 p.m. PST:

  • Mega Level 1 or higher: Moonblast+ has boosted base power (not in GO Battle League).
  • Super Max Level: Mega Clefable has boosted combat power.

Where to Find Super Mega Raids

Super Mega Raids take teamwork and only appear at certain Gyms, often in parks and similar locations. The official Pokémon GO map shows where Super Mega Raids might appear during the event, plus raids in progress.

You can also filter the map or check nearby events to find community meetups days in advance. Many are hosted by Community Ambassadors, and you can find your local community here. If you’ve never been to a meetup, a Super Mega Raid Day is a great first one.

item.content:encoded:
GO Wild Area 2026: Mexico City takes place on November 6, 7 and 8, from 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. local time each day, with gameplay throughout Mexico City, Mexico. Gigantamax Duraludon debuts in six-star Max Battles, Dynamax Dialga and Dynamax Palkia make their Dynamax debuts, and mighty Pokémon return. Steel- and Dragon-type Pokémon take the spotlight, Hisuian Sliggoo and Hisuian Goodra arrive, and Machamp gets a new look!

This is a ticketed, in-person event. A one-day ticket costs MXN$350, plus applicable taxes and fees, and gives you access to event gameplay on your chosen day. Optional Extra Day Add-ons let you extend your visit. Ticket holders can look forward to extra bonuses, Steel- and Dragon-themed Special Research, and a chance to encounter mighty Latias and Latios from Incense.

Around Mexico City during Pokémon GO Wild Area there is not only gameplay to look forward to, but you can also meet Pokémon, artists, and community leaders, visit special locations, and take part in activities across the city. Here’s what to know before you go.

Map

Meet Pokémon!

Pikachu and Eevee will appear at Pokémon GO Wild Area: Mexico City for meet-and-greet opportunities at the Monumento a la Revolución. Trainers can stop by during the scheduled times below for photos and a special Pokémon GO moment.

Dates and Location

  • Location: Monumento a la Revolución
  • Dates: November 6–8, 2026

Times (All times listed are in CST)

  • 10:00 a.m. to 12:50 p.m.
  • Break from 1:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m.
  • 3:00 p.m. to 5:50 p.m.

Meet-and-greet times may change or be canceled due to weather or other unforeseen circumstances.

Meet Notable Trainers

Ticket-holding Trainers can meet notable Trainers from the Pokémon GO community at Monumento a la Revolución. Lines may be capped early if necessary.

Dates and Location

Dates: November 6–8, 2026
Location: Monumento a la Revolución

Times and Trainers

From 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. each day:

  • Neludia
  • Alex y Tely
  • Martogalde

From 2:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. each day:

  • Keibron Gamer
  • The Trainer Club
  • Rochababyface

Trainer Statues

  • Dates: November 6–8, 2026
  • Locations: Several locations around Mexico City.

Trainers can find life-sized statues of the team leaders at several locations around Mexico City. These statues are available as photo opportunities while Trainers explore the city and check out other Pokémon GO Wild Area activities.

Community Ambassador Meetups

  • Dates: November 6–8, 2026
  • Location: Parque México

At Parque México, Community Ambassadors have a set place to meet up with their local communities, and new communities. New players can also find activities and learn more about the Community Ambassador and Wayfarer programs, including how to get involved with their local Pokémon GO community.

Player Support and Belonging Booth

  • Dates: November 6–8, 2026
  • Location: Jardín Pushkin

At Jardín Pushkin, Trainers can visit the Player Support tent with questions about their game experience. The Belonging Booth will provide a safe and welcoming space for neurodivergent players and players with disabilities, as well as family services. Trainers can also learn more about the support and accommodations available at the event.

Meet the Artists

  • Dates: November 6–8, 2026
  • Location: Jardín Pushkin

At Jardín Pushkin, Trainers will be able to meet artists who work on Pokémon GO and learn more about the people behind the game’s art.

Friday, November 6

  • 10:00 a.m. – 12:00 p.m.: Jonathan Glabas and Jason Marino
  • 2:00 p.m. – 4:00 p.m.: Kaan Kayimoglu and Jose Deschamps

Saturday, November 7

  • 10:00 a.m. – 12:00 p.m.: Jason Marino and Kaan Kayimoglu
  • 12:30 p.m. – 1:30 p.m.: Join Jason Marino, Senior 3D Artist, who will be hosting a conference at Cinépolis Diana to discuss the process of bringing art to life in Pokémon GO.
  • 2:00 p.m. – 4:00 p.m.: Jason Marino and Jose Deschamps

Sunday, November 8

  • 10:00 a.m. – 12:00 p.m.: Jonathan Glabas and Jose Deschamps
  • 2:00 p.m. – 4:00 p.m.: Kaan Kayimoglu and Jonathan Glabas

Times and participants may change.

Mexicráneos

  • Dates: November 6–8, 2026
  • Location: Paseo de la Reforma, near El Ángel de la Independencia

Pokémon GO will return to Paseo de la Reforma as part of Mexicráneos. Inspired by Día de Muertos and designed in collaboration with Mexican artists, the two installations are recognizable photo opportunities for visitors.

Both of the Pokemon GO Mexicráneos will be located near El Ángel de la Independencia. One of them will also be one of the stops in the Día de Muertos Stamp Rally.

Parque Hundido Activation

  • Dates: November 6–8, 2026
  • Location: Parque Hundido

Parque Hundido is one of the local community’s favorite places to play. Trainers can stop by for photo opportunities and pick up Pikachu visors while supplies last.

Cinépolis Collaboration

  • Dates: November 5–9, 2026
  • Location: Cinépolis Diana

Cinépolis Diana, located next to the Diana Cazadora statue on Paseo de la Reforma, will host a Pokémon GO Wild Area takeover.

Trainers visiting the location can enjoy photo opportunities and event decorations inside the theater. Event-themed disposable coasters will also be available with select purchases while supplies last.

Cinépolis ticket-holder benefits will also be available only to Pokémon GO Wild Area ticket holders. Details about that benefit will be shared separately by email.

Liverpool Polanco

  • Dates: November 5–9, 2026
  • Location: Cinépolis Diana

Trainers visiting Liverpool Polanco can find Pokémon GO photo opportunities during the weekend. Pikachu visors will also be distributed at the location while supplies last.

Pikachu, Hawlucha, and Machamp Sun Visor Distribution

  • Dates: November 6–8, 2026
  • Locations: Monumento a la Revolución; Parque México; Jardín Pushkin; Cinépolis Diana; Liverpool Polanco; Parque Hundido

Trainers can pick up a Pikachu, Hawlucha, or Machamp sun visor to add some fun to their journey while exploring Mexico City.

Distribution times may vary by location. Quantities at each location are limited. Visors will be distributed on a first-come, first-served basis while supplies last.

Turibús Collaboration

  • Dates: November 6–8, 2026
  • Location: Mexico City

Explore Mexico City on Turibús’s Centro Histórico, Sur, and Polanco circuits, with stops near event activations and an additional temporary stop for Liverpool Polanco during the event days.

Show your Pokémon GO Wild Area: Mexico City in-game medal when purchasing tickets in person to receive a discounted rate. Discount not available online.

Also, keep an eye out for a special Pokémon GO Wild Area–themed Turibús! View routes and more information on the Turibús website: https://www.turibus.com.mx/cdmx.

BBVA Collaboration

  • Dates: November 6–8, 2026
  • Locations: BBVA Tower and the Pokémon GO Wild Area pop-up store

A special surprise will light up BBVA Tower to celebrate Pokémon GO Wild Area: Mexico City. Catch it from 6:00 p.m. to midnight on November 6–8.

At the pop-up store, Trainers who pay with any BBVA card can use a priority checkout lane and receive one Pokémon GO keychain or pin while supplies last.

Limit one gift item per customer.

Pop-Up Shop and Pre-Order Collection

  • Location: Foro Reforma, Calle Lucerna #70, Juárez, Cuauhtémoc, 06600 Ciudad de México, CDMX
  • Dates: November 6–8, 2026
  • Hours: 10:00 a.m. – 7:00 p.m.

Trainers who preordered merchandise can pick it up at the Pokémon GO Wild Area pop-up store.

A limited quantity of additional merchandise will also be available for purchase without a preorder. These items will be available on a first-come, first-served basis while supplies last.

Pokémon GO Across Mexico City

  • Dates: November 1–23, 2026
  • Location: Mexico City

From November 1–23, Trainers may see Pokémon GO Wild Area: Mexico City advertising across the city, including Metro and Metrobús stations, Ecobici locations, and other public spaces. Keep an eye out for the team leaders and other Pokémon GO Wild Area decorations as you travel around Mexico City.

item.content:encoded:
Dynamax Dialga 2217 CP / 2307 CP

Dynamax Dialga is a Legendary Dragon and Steel type Pokémon appearing in Tier 5 Max Battles, costing 800 Max Particles (MP) per successful battle. It is weak to Fighting and Ground-type attacks.

 Its catch CP ranges from 2217 to 2307 CP.

You can only battle Dynamax Dialga in teams of 4, so be sure to build your teams ahead of time and use appropriate counters.

Dynamax Dialga Counters

Recommended Team

  • Crowned Shield Zamazenta Metal Claw
  • Dynamax Blissey Pound
  • Gigantamax Machamp G-Max Chi Strike
  • Zamazenta is your best option as a defender for Dialga. Backed up by Blissey as a healer this will work very well. 
  • Gigantamax Machamp is the clear best attacker for Dialga.

Best Attackers for Dynamax Dialga

The best attackers for defeating Dynamax Dialga are the following Pokémon:

  • Gigantamax Machamp G-Max Chi Strike
  • Urshifu Either Max Knuckle
  • Dynamax Excadrill Max Quake
  • Dynamax Rhyperior Max Quake
  • Dynamax Gallade Max Knuckle
  • Dynamax Machamp Max Knuckle

Your best attacking option is Eternatus. After that your most powerful options from the list above will serve you well.

Best Defenders for Dynamax Dialga

The best defenders to use against a Dynamax Dialga are the following Pokémon:

  • Crowned Shield Zamazenta Metal Claw
  • Crowned Sword Zacian Metal Claw
  • Dynamax Registeel Lock On / Metal Claw
  • Dynamax Metagross Fury Cutter /Shadow Claw
  • Dynamax Regirock Lock On
  • Dynamax Regice Lock On
  • Zamazenta is the best defender for Dialga as it resists Dialga’s attacks whilst charging up the max meter as quickly as possible.

Best Healers for Dynamax Dialga

The best healers to use in a Dynamax Dialga Max Battle are the following Pokémon:

  • Dynamax Blissey
  • Dynamax Wailord
  • Dynamax Snorlax
  • Gigantamax Lapras
  • Dynamax Vaporeon
  • Eternatus

Team Composition

Dynamax Battles can be participated in by up to 4 Trainers.  In each group of 4 we recommend two Trainers have teams focused on attackers, one tank/defender team, and one healer team.

Your team of 3 Pokémon should begin with a Charger, a Pokémon with a 0.5s fast move, and then two optimal attacker Pokémon.

Your Charger Pokémon should come from this list of Pokémon with 0.5s fast moves. The quicker your fast move, the quicker you can charge to the Dynamax phase. When you Dynamax, swap to your attacker, then swap back.

Remember, your Fast Move determines your attack typing in your Dynamax Phase, which is why we haven’t included any recommended Charged Moves.

Dynamax Dialga Shiny Comparison

Regular Sprite Shiny Sprite
Dialga Dialga

Dynamax Dialga Movepool

Fast Moves Charge Moves
  • Dragon Breath Dragon
  • Metal Claw Steel
  • Iron Head Steel
  • Draco Meteor Dragon
  • Thunder Electric 

Frequently Asked Questions

How to charge up your Max Meter?

In a Dynamax Battle, tap the screen to use Fast Attacks as fast as possible, and to fill up the Max Meter at the top of the screen. Your Max Meter is filled depending on how much damage you do, but never less than 1 Max Energy.

How to dodge Boss Attacks

When three lines appear above a Pokemon’s head, it means it is being targeted by the Max Battle Boss. You can avoid this by swiping to either the left or the right.

The Dynamax Phase

When your Max Meter reaches its maximum, your Pokémon will automatically Dynamax/Gigantamax. You can fill it up by swiping towards the energy icons that appears from time to time, or by using your Fast and Charged Attacks. Once it is full, your Pokémon will Dynamax for 3 turns.

  • You have a 3 second countdown to choose the Pokémon you wish to Dynamax / Gigantamax. You can pick any Pokémon, but it depends on which role you are fulfilling in your group. 
  • Once your Dynamax Phase ends you can immediately switch back to another Pokémon in your team if you wish to.
  • You can Dynamax more than once in a Max Battle, and will automatically Dynamax once your Max Meter refills.

If all of your Pokémon faint while battling a 3-star or higher level Boss with other Trainers, you can still help your allies by cheering for your them so that their meters fill faster.

It is also worth communicating with your fellow Trainers to ensure that those who may be less prepared, such as children who don’t have the resources of others, are included in groups that can help carry them through.

Max Guard

Max Guard can be used to add a maximum of 3 shields to your Pokémon. How much HP a single shield can absorb depends on the Max Guard level.

  • 20HP for level 1
  • 40HP for level 2
  • 60 HP for level 3

When stacked to a maximum of 3 shields it gives you:

  • 60HP for level 1
  • 120HP for level 2
  • 180HP for level 3

If you find you are re-entering your Dynamax Phase and you still have shields left, it would be recommended to top back up to 3 shields, then use your Max Attack for your other moves.

While shields are only applied to the Pokémon using them, it is a hugely important aspect of a Max Battle. Whilst shielded, the Max Battle boss will direct its focused attacks towards the Pokémon that is shielded only!

The defender therefore draws damage away from the other active Pokémon in battle, protecting them from the more powerful Max Battle attack. Dodging should still be attempted in order to reduce the damage received and keep your shields up for longer. We cannot under-estimate how important Max Guard is due to it drawing damage away for your whole group, it is absolutely key to utilise in your strategy.

Only one person in your group of four needs to use Max Guard, so communication is key here.

Max Spirit

Max Spirit heals not only Pokémon using it, but also any other active Pokémon on the battle field in your group of 4. The amount of health restored is based on the level of Max Spirit and the user’s maximum HP. Aim to level up your Max Spirit to at least level 2 for a dedicated healer.

This means that Pokémon with high stamina and HP stats are better healers, even if they don’t have optimal attacks for their Max Battle boss.

Attackers in Max Battles

Attackers are Pokémon that have Max Attack levelled up. Attackers in Max Battles are the Pokémon you want to use during the Dynamax Phase. These Pokémon deal maximum damage to the Max Boss.

Remember, in Max Battles your Fast Move that determines the typing of your Max Move, so it is key to ensure it has the correct typing that will deal super effective damage to the boss. Attackers are recommended based on their typings, and their attack stats.

Defenders in Max Battles

Defenders are Pokémon that have Max Guard leveled up. Good defenders are Pokémon who have large defense and stamina stats, and take reduced damage from the Max Boss. This enables you to stay alive longer, and charge up your Max Meter faster.

Defenders are recommended based on having high level defense and stamina stats, along with their typing being resistant to the Max Bosses potential moveset.

Healers in Max Battles

item.content:encoded:
Dynamax Palkia 2190 CP / 2280 CP

Dynamax Palkia is a Legendary Dragon and Water type Pokémon appearing in Tier 5 Max Battles, costing 800 Max Particles (MP) per successful battle. It is weak to Dragon, and Fairy-type attacks.

 Its catch CP ranges from 2190 to 2280 CP.

Palkia does have a very strong Fire, Water and Dragon move available which makes defending very tricky. Please note that if Palkia has Fire Blast as a target move this will really hurt Registeel and Zamazenta. If Palkia has Hydro Pump as a target move it will really hurt Regirock and if Palkia has Draco Meteor it will really hurt Suicune, Blastoise and Palkia. We would suggest bringing a combination of defenders into the max battle within your team and then deciding on who should take the defending role once the moves have been ascertained.

You can only battle Dynamax Palkia in teams of 4, so be sure to build your teams ahead of time and use appropriate counters.

Dynamax Palkia Counters

Recommended Team

  • Dynamax Suicune Water Gun
  • Dynamax Blissey Pound
  • Eternatus Dynamax Cannon
  • Suicune is your best option as a defender for Palkia. Backed up by Blissey as a healer this will work very well. 
  • Eternatus is the clear best attacker for Palkia.

Best Attackers for Dynamax Palkia

The best attackers for defeating Dynamax Palkia are the following Pokémon:

  • Eternatus Dynamax Cannon
  • Gigantamax Duraludon G-Max Depletion
  • Dynamax Palkia Max Wyrmwind
  • Dynamax Dialga Max Wyrmwind
  • Dynamax Latios Max Wyrmwind
  • Dynamax Hydreigon Max Wyrmwind

Your best attacking option is Eternatus. After that your most powerful options from the list above will serve you well.

Best Defenders for Dynamax Palkia

The best defenders to use against a Dynamax Palkia are the following Pokémon:

  • Dynamax Suicune Water Gun
  • Crowned Shield Zamazenta Metal Claw
  • Dynamax Blastoise Water Gun /Bite
  • Dynamax Palkia Dragon Breath
  • Dynamax Registeel Lock On / Metal Claw
  • Dynamax Regirock Lock-On
  • While these are the recommended defenders, Palkia does have a very strong Fire, Water and Dragon move available which makes defending very tricky. Please note that if Palkia has Fire Blast as a target move this will really hurt Registeel and Zamazenta. If Palkia has Hydro Pump as a target move it will really hurt Regirock and if Palkia has Draco Meteor it will really hurt Suicune, Blastoise and Palkia. We would suggest bringing a combination of defenders into the max battle within your team and then deciding on who should take the defending role once the moves have been ascertained.

Best Healers for Dynamax Palkia

The best healers to use in a Dynamax Palkia Max Battle are the following Pokémon:

  • Dynamax Blissey
  • Dynamax Wailord
  • Dynamax Snorlax
  • Gigantamax Lapras
  • Dynamax Vaporeon
  • Eternatus

Team Composition

Dynamax Battles can be participated in by up to 4 Trainers.  In each group of 4 we recommend two Trainers have teams focused on attackers, one tank/defender team, and one healer team.

Your team of 3 Pokémon should begin with a Charger, a Pokémon with a 0.5s fast move, and then two optimal attacker Pokémon.

Your Charger Pokémon should come from this list of Pokémon with 0.5s fast moves. The quicker your fast move, the quicker you can charge to the Dynamax phase. When you Dynamax, swap to your attacker, then swap back.

Remember, your Fast Move determines your attack typing in your Dynamax Phase, which is why we haven’t included any recommended Charged Moves.

Dynamax Palkia Shiny Comparison

Regular Sprite Shiny Sprite
Palkia Palkia

Fast Moves Charge Moves
  • Dragon Breath Dragon
  • Dragon Tail Dragon
  • Fire Blast Fire
  • Draco Meteor Dragon

  • Aqua Tail Water

Frequently Asked Questions

How to charge up your Max Meter?

In a Dynamax Battle, tap the screen to use Fast Attacks as fast as possible, and to fill up the Max Meter at the top of the screen. Your Max Meter is filled depending on how much damage you do, but never less than 1 Max Energy.

How to dodge Boss Attacks

When three lines appear above a Pokémon’s head, it means it is being targeted by the Max Battle Boss. You can avoid this by swiping to either the left or the right.

The Dynamax Phase

When your Max Meter reaches its maximum, your Pokémon will automatically Dynamax/Gigantamax. You can fill it up by swiping towards the energy icons that appears from time to time, or by using your Fast and Charged Attacks. Once it is full, your Pokémon will Dynamax for 3 turns.

  • You have a 3 second countdown to choose the Pokémon you wish to Dynamax / Gigantamax. You can pick any Pokémon, but it depends on which role you are fulfilling in your group. 
  • Once your Dynamax Phase ends you can immediately switch back to another Pokémon in your team if you wish to.
  • You can Dynamax more than once in a Max Battle, and will automatically Dynamax once your Max Meter refills.

If all of your Pokémon faint while battling a 3-star or higher level Boss with other Trainers, you can still help your allies by cheering for your them so that their meters fill faster.

It is also worth communicating with your fellow Trainers to ensure that those who may be less prepared, such as children who don’t have the resources of others, are included in groups that can help carry them through.

Max Guard

Max Guard can be used to add a maximum of 3 shields to your Pokémon. How much HP a single shield can absorb depends on the Max Guard level.

  • 20HP for level 1
  • 40HP for level 2
  • 60 HP for level 3

When stacked to a maximum of 3 shields it gives you:

  • 60HP for level 1
  • 120HP for level 2
  • 180HP for level 3

If you find you are re-entering your Dynamax Phase and you still have shields left, it would be recommended to top back up to 3 shields, then use your Max Attack for your other moves.

While shields are only applied to the Pokémon using them, it is a hugely important aspect of a Max Battle. Whilst shielded, the Max Battle boss will direct its focused attacks towards the Pokémon that is shielded only!

The defender therefore draws damage away from the other active Pokémon in battle, protecting them from the more powerful Max Battle attack. Dodging should still be attempted in order to reduce the damage received and keep your shields up for longer. We cannot under-estimate how important Max Guard is due to it drawing damage away for your whole group, it is absolutely key to utilise in your strategy.

Only one person in your group of four needs to use Max Guard, so communication is key here.

Max Spirit

Max Spirit heals not only Pokémon using it, but also any other active Pokémon on the battle field in your group of 4. The amount of health restored is based on the level of Max Spirit and the user’s maximum HP. Aim to level up your Max Spirit to at least level 2 for a dedicated healer.

This means that Pokémon with high stamina and HP stats are better healers, even if they don’t have optimal attacks for their Max Battle boss.

Attackers in Max Battles

Attackers are Pokémon that have Max Attack levelled up. Attackers in Max Battles are the Pokémon you want to use during the Dynamax Phase. These Pokémon deal maximum damage to the Max Boss.

Remember, in Max Battles your Fast Move that determines the typing of your Max Move, so it is key to ensure it has the correct typing that will deal super effective damage to the boss. Attackers are recommended based on their typings, and their attack stats.

Defenders in Max Battles

Defenders are Pokémon that have Max Guard leveled up. Good defenders are Pokémon who have large defense and stamina stats, and take reduced damage from the Max Boss. This enables you to stay alive longer, and charge up your Max Meter faster.

Defenders are recommended based on having high level defense and stamina stats, along with their typing being resistant to the Max Bosses potential moveset.

Healers in Max Battles

Healers are Pokémon that have Max Spirit levelled up. Healers are used in the max phase to apply healing to your team. Healers are recommended based on their stamina stat. Other elements are considered, including their ability to pull double duty as defenders or attackers.

Dynamax Azelf Psychic

Dynamax Azelf is one of the Lake Trio Legendary Pokémon that debuted recently, alongside Mesprit and Uxie. It also marked the first time ever a Max Pokémon is region-locked, as Azelf is only be available in Americas and Greenland region.

Of the three, Azelf represents the more attack-oriented one that trades off DEF and HP for a massive ATK value of 270 – the highest of the Lake Guardian trio by a wide margin. Just by looking at its ATK value, it makes sense to be hopeful that Azelf gets ranked highly compared to other Psychic attackers. At the same time, it is understandable that Azelf should never be utilized defensively, after all, no one should bring a Pokémon with 151 DEF, who lacks a 0.5s fast attack move into Max Battles as a tank.

As an Attacker: A Premium Psychic-type Damage Dealer

At 270 ATK, Dynamax Azelf lands at #2 among current Psychic damage dealers, a mere 0.4% behind Dynamax Alakazam – a gap so close that it can be interpreted in two completely contradictory ways.

On one hand, it can be argued that Azelf is the co-best Psychic attacker in the current meta, with its damage output so similar to Alakazam’s, and thus making it worth farming for during its debut Max Battle Day event, especially for trainers who want a team filled with Legendaries and Mythicals.

On the other, Azelf being region-locked to the Americas and Greenland means that it can get extremely costly to farm one up, particularly for those who don’t live in these regions, unless they plan to use Rare Candies / Rare Candy XL to max one out; thus it makes a lot more financial sense to build up an Alakazam instead.

The final choice differs from trainer to trainer, depending on their resources; but either way, despite ranking really high as a Psychic damage dealer, in the long run, Azelf will slip down to #8, trailing behind a series of other Legendaries and Mythicals, such as Deoxys (Attack Forme) at +50%, Deoxys (Normal Forme) at +26%, Hoopa Unbound at +14%, and Mewtwo at +10%… None of them has a Dynamax form yet, so Azelf still has some rooms to breathe for now.

: Is Azelf The Best Choice Against Every Typing That Is Weak to Psychic?

While being arguably the co-best Psychic attacker with Alakazam, it is also worth comparing Dynamax Azelf against other typings that also deal super effective damage to Fighting and Poison-type Pokémon to ultimately conclude whether the Being of Willpower is indeed the ultimate choice that is worth serious investment into.

The table below compares Dynamax Azelf against the top damage dealers across every type that deals Super Effective damage to either Fighting or Poison-type Pokémon.

Ranking Pokémon Damage Type Max Attack Damage vs. D-Max Azelf
1 Dynamax Azelf –
2 Dynamax Excadrill -5.3%

4 Dynamax Rhyperior -10.2%
5 Dynamax Gardevoir -11.6%
5 Dynamax Hatterene -11.6%

vs. Fighting (weak to , , )

Azelf is comfortably distance ahead of the current #1 Flying-type attacker i.e. Dynamax Moltres, and current #1 Fairy-type attacker i.e. Dynamax Gardevoir and Dynamax Hatterene, making it the current best counter to any Fighting-type Pokémon in Max Battles.

vs. Poison (weak to , )

Azelf also comes out on top by at least 5% ahead of the current top Ground-type attackers i.e. Dynamax Excadrill and Dynamax Rhyperior, making it also the best choice in the current meta when dealing with any Poison-type Pokémon in Max Battles.

Verdict: A Near-S-rank Psychic Attacker

Dynamax Azelf is the only Lake Guardian that earns a spot at the top of the attacker ranking, sitting just a hair behind Dynamax Alakazam and ahead of every other current Psychic attacker. Azelf does its attacking role so well that it is arguably the co-best damage dealer against Fighting and Poison-type Pokémon, pushing ahead by at least 5% compared to Flying, Fairy and Ground attackers.

This makes Azelf the most worth it to farm among the Lake Guardian trios. It is, however, worth noting that Azelf remains a premium investment unless you are loaded with Rare Candies / Rare Candy XL. Alakazam could do a very similar job with much less pressure on farming up candies. Nevertheless, if you decide to go for it, farm out a 15 ATK IV and enjoy a premium Psychic attacker that will stay relevant for a long time.

Dynamax Uxie is one of the Lake Trio Legendary Pokémon that debuted recently, alongside Azelf and Mesprit. It also marked the first time ever a Max Pokémon was region-locked, as Uxie will only be available in Asia-Pacific region.

Of the three, Uxie represents the tankier one with a massive DEF stat of 270, but with a relatively low HP value of 181 and really mediocre ATK stat of 156. Coupled with the fact that none of the Lake Trio has access to a 0.5s fast attack move, it really seems bleak for Uxie to be able to break into anything in the Max meta. Either way, let’s see if Uxie’s high DEF is enough to earn a spot on your Max team, or whether it is just a high number on a stat sheet.

The top five, led by Alakazam, all hit somewhere 60-67% harder than the Being of Knowledge itself. And obviously, if it is already performing this badly in the attacking front in the current meta, there is clearly nothing futureproof to Uxie in this area. You are just much better off using other Psychic damage dealers than getting Uxie as one.

As a Tank: Just a Good Tank on Paper

At 270 DEF value, naturally this is Dynamax Uxie‘s territory… or rather, this should have been its territory.

However, its poor HP value pulls its overall tankiness down, as in the long run when all Pokémon makes their debut in Max Battles, Uxie will badly fall out of the lead, and rank at best #33 tank against Psychic. What makes matters worse for Uxie is that it is also missing a 0.5s Fast Attack. The farming value for Uxie this weekend is arguably only to farm for stardust, and farm for a shiny if you are lucky. Otherwise, if you care less about either of this, sadly it might be much more worth it to go for its siblings, i.e. Azelf and Mesprit.

Is It Worth Evolving Teddiursa?

PVE

Ursaluna is a rather unique Pokémon in how you obtain it. To evolve an Ursaring into Ursaluna, you must do this on the night of a full moon with 100 candies, meaning you have just one night a month to get this powerful bear.

Raids

Ursaluna, while decent one time in the past, has been outclassed by A LOT of other Pokémon. Its biggest problem is it doesn’t have a Ground-type fast attack, so it can only rely on Tackle, along with the legacy move High Horsepower. As such, it just can’t do enough damage consistently as a Ground-type raid attacker and falls behind. There isn’t any reason to use it as a Normal-type raid attacker either, as no Pokémon are weak to Normal-types.

Gyms

This bear is just right to sit on gyms and earn you some Pokécoins. Due to its impressive bulk and high CP, it can be a formidable wall for trainers to beat, especially if paired with some diverse type matchups.

Ursaluna isn’t a good enough Pokémon to be under your radar for your primary meta-dominant team. This mostly comes down to the fact it doesn’t reach its best stat potential under 1500 CP. However, it does have a rather diverse movepool, and a decent fast attack in Scratch. As such, you could consider using it if you want to use it as a spice/limited meta pick.

Ultra League

The exact same applies to Ursaluna in the Ultra League.

Master League

Here’s where Ursaluna can shine bright as the moon that helped it evolve. As it already has high Attack and a lower Defense stat, it outperforms its Shadow counterpart. Heck, its low defense stat doesn’t even matter here, as Ursaluna’s sheer HP in the league makes it extremely bulky. Its diverse movepool means you can give it charged attacks you need to deal with the limitations of your team. All of this is to say, Ursaluna is one of the rare non-legendaries that dominate the Master League and you should definitely consider building one for it.

  • Your best G-Max Duraludon counter is Gigantamax Machamp. G-Max Machamp is the strongest Fighting-type attacker available at the moment. 
  • After Machamp, pick your most powerful options from the list above, and they will serve you well.
  • * denotes an elite TM is required

Attackers in Max Battles

Attackers are Pokémon that have Max Attack levelled up. Attackers in Max Battles are the Pokémon you want to use during the Dynamax Phase. These Pokémon deal maximum damage to the Max Boss.

Remember, in Max Battles your Fast Move that determines the typing of your Max Move, so it is key to ensure it has the correct typing that will deal super effective damage to the boss. Attackers are recommended based on their typings, and their attack stats.

Best Defenders for Gigantamax Duraludon

The best defenders to use against a Gigantamax Duraludon are the following Pokémon:

# Pokémon Fast Move
1. Crowned Shield Zamazenta
  • Metal Claw
2. Registeel Dynamax
  • Lock On / Metal Claw
3. Metagross Dynamax
  • Fury Cutter /Shadow Claw*
4. Crowned Sword Zacian
  • Metal Claw
5. Corviknight Dynamax
  • Sand Attack
6. Dialga Dynamax
  • Dragon Breath / Metal Claw
  • Zamazenta is your top choice, as it is resistant to what Duraludon has to offer whilst still charging up the Max Meter as quickly as possible.
  • *denotes an elite TM is required!

Defenders in Max Battles

Defenders are Pokémon that have Max Guard levelled up. Good defenders are Pokémon who have large defense and stamina stats, and take reduced damage from the Max Boss. This enables you to stay alive longer, and charge up your Max Meter faster.

Defenders are recommended based on having high level defense and stamina stats, along with their typing being resistant to the Max Bosses potential moveset.

Best Healers for Gigantamax Duraludon

The best healers to use in a Gigantamax Duraludon Max Battle are the following Pokémon:

  • Dynamax Blissey
  • Dynamax Wailord
  • Dynamax Snorlax
  • Gigantamax Lapras
  • Dynamax Vaporeon
  • Eternatus

Ideally, you want a Blissey. Wailord, Snorlax, or Lapras are great second choices however.

Team Composition

Gigantamax Battles can be participated in by up to 40 Trainers. Those 40 Trainers are then split up into groups of 4 that work together. In each group of 4 we recommend two Trainers have teams focused on attackers, one tank/defender team, and one healer team.

Your team of 3 Pokémon should begin with a Charger, a Pokémon with a 0.5s fast move, and then two optimal attacker Pokémon.

Your Charger Pokémon should come from this list of Pokémon with 0.5s fast moves. The quicker your fast move, the quicker you can charge to the Dynamax phase. When you Dynamax, swap to your attacker, then swap back.

Remember, your Fast Move determines your attack typing in your Dynamax Phase, which is why we haven’t included any recommended Charged Moves.

Gigantamax Duraludon Movepool

Fast Moves Charge Moves
  • Dragon Tail Dragon
  • Metal Claw Steel
  • Flash Cannon Steel 
  • Dragon Claw Dragon
  • Hyper Beam Normal 

Gigantamax Bosses use 2 charged moves from their movepool, which can include legacy moves:

  • One attack will damage all Pokémon currently active in battle and cannot be dodged.
  • The other is as a more powerful attack that targets only one of the active Pokémon.

The single-target move deals double the regular damage, but it can be dodged by swiping when you get the warning above your Pokémon. They do not use any of their Fast Moves.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why do we recommend not using Charged Moves in Gigantamax Battles

We don’t recommend using any Charge Moves in Gigantamax Battles. The main reasons we recommend not using charged moves during Gigantamax Battles are as follows:

  • The amount of Max Energy generated per attack is based on damage dealt in relation to the maximum HP of the Gigantamax Boss, but has a minimum value of 1, because the formula uses rounding.
  • Because of how bulky these Gigantamax Bosses are, there are no charged moves that can generate more than 1 Max Energy per use. In other words, you are losing time using Charge moves.
  • Since the execution time of Fast Moves are a lot quicker than those of Charged Moves (charged attacks have a much slower animation), yet they generate the same amount of Max Energy, using only Fast Moves fills up the Max Meter faster.

For Gigantamax battles and Legendary Dynamax battles, using only fast moves is the best strategy. Be sure to advise your fellow Trainers of this when meeting up with your local community to optimise this strategy!

How Gigantamax Battles work

To participate in a Gigantamax Battles you either have to:

  • be there in-person, at Power Spots, which are easily identified on the map by the purple marking and large ‘X’ above them,
  • or join Remotely.

You can take up Gigantamax Battles with up to 40 people, which will be divided into groups of 4 Trainers.

  • Each person can bring up to three Pokémon in their team
  • Only Pokémon that can Dynamax or Gigantamax can participate in Max Battles
  • Max Battles are turn based, differing from both raiding and GO Battle League. 

How to charge up your Max Meter?

In a Gigantamax Battle, tap the screen to use Fast Attacks as fast as possible, and ti fill up the Max Meter at the top of the screen. Your Max Meter is filled depending on how much damage you do, but never less than 1 Max Energy.

Since Gigantamax Bosses have incredibly high stats, it is not worth using Charge Moves – you are better off using Fast Moves. This is quite different from Dynamax Battles, so be careful.

How to dodge Boss Attacks

When three lines appear above a Pokemon’s head, it means it is being targeted by the Max Battle Boss. You can avoid this by swiping to either the left or the right.

The Dynamax Phase

When your Max Meter reaches its maximum, your Pokémon will automatically Dynamax/Gigantamax. You can fill it up by swiping towards the energy icons that appears from time to time, or by using your Fast and Charged Attacks. Once it is full, your Pokémon will Dynamax for 3 turns.

  • You have a 3 second countdown to choose the Pokémon you wish to Dynamax / Gigantamax. You can pick any Pokémon, but it depends on which role you are fulfilling in your group. 
  • Once your Dynamax Phase ends you can immediately switch back to another Pokémon in your team if you wish to.
  • You can Dynamax more than once in a Max Battle, and will automatically Dynamax once your Max Meter refills.

If all of your Pokémon faint while battling a 3-star or higher level Boss with other Trainers, you can still help your allies by cheering for your them so that their meters fill faster.

Best Group Composition for Gigantamax Battles

For Gigantamax battles a maximum of 40 Trainers can enter the battle together, in lobbies of 4 Trainers. Generally, the best strategy for each group of 4 is to have :

  • 2 attackers
  • 1 defender
  • 1 healer

This will allow your group to stay alive as long as possible, whilst also directing damage towards one specific trainer, and allowing maximum damage to take place.

It is advisable to keep in mind that Trainers are grouped together in the order of joining the lobby, so it may be worth planning to ensure that the most prepared Trainers with leveled up Max Spirit and Max Guard are paired with others who are only prepared for attacks.

It is also worth communicating with your fellow Trainers to ensure that those who may be less prepared, such as children who don’t have the resources of others, are included in groups that can help carry them through.

Max Guard

Max Guard can be used to add a maximum of 3 shields to your Pokémon. How much HP a single shield can absorb depends on the Max Guard level.

  • 20HP for level 1
  • 40HP for level 2
  • 60 HP for level 3

When stacked to a maximum of 3 shields it gives you:

  • 60HP for level 1
  • 120HP for level 2
  • 180HP for level 3

If you find you are re-entering your Dynamax Phase and you still have shields left, it would be recommended to top back up to 3 shields, then use your Max Attack for your other moves.

While shields are only applied to the Pokémon using them, it is a hugely important aspect of a Max Battle. Whilst shielded, the Max Battle boss will direct its focused attacks towards the Pokémon that is shielded only!

The defender therefore draws damage away from the other active Pokémon in battle, protecting them from the more powerful Max Battle attack. Dodging should still be attempted in order to reduce the damage received and keep your shields up for longer. We cannot under-estimate how important Max Guard is due to it drawing damage away for your whole group, it is absolutely key to utilise in your strategy.

Only one person in your group of four needs to use Max Guard, so communication is key here.

Max Spirit

Max Spirit heals not only Pokémon using it, but also any other active Pokémon on the battle field in your group of 4. The amount of health restored is based on the level of Max Spirit and the user’s maximum HP. Aim to level up your Max Spirit to at least level 2 for a dedicated healer.

This means that Pokémon with high stamina and HP stats are better healers, even if they don’t have optimal attacks for their Max Battle boss.

Attackers in Max Battles

Attackers are Pokémon that have Max Attack levelled up. Attackers in Max Battles are the Pokémon you want to use during the Dynamax Phase. These Pokémon deal maximum damage to the Max Boss.

Remember, in Max Battles your Fast Move that determines the typing of your Max Move, so it is key to ensure it has the correct typing that will deal super effective damage to the boss. Attackers are recommended based on their typings, and their attack stats.

Defenders in Max Battles

Defenders are Pokémon that have Max Guard leveled up. Good defenders are Pokémon who have large defense and stamina stats, and take reduced damage from the Max Boss. This enables you to stay alive longer, and charge up your Max Meter faster.

Defenders are recommended based on having high level defense and stamina stats, along with their typing being resistant to the Max Bosses potential moveset.

Healers in Max Battles

Healers are Pokémon that have Max Spirit levelled up. Healers are used in the max phase to apply healing to your team. Healers are recommended based on their stamina stat. Other elements are considered, including their ability to pull double duty as defenders or attackers.

Shadow Tornadus Incarnate takes over Shadow Raids in Pokémon GO, and as expected, speculation is rife about its meta viability as a Flying type. Unlike the other Legendary Genies (except Enamorus), Tornadus Incarnate is particularly interesting given that it’s the only Incarnate Forme (among the original Gen 5 Genies) whose ATK stat is higher than the Therian Forme.

Shadow Tornadus Therian has the advantage of higher ATK, that is firther boosted due to the Shadow effect. On the other hand, the Therian Forme learns Bleakwind Storm. It is also the signature move for Tornadus, and unfortunately, only the Therian forms learn these signature moves in Pokémon GO.

So who ends up getting the upper hand, and how does Shadow Tornadus Incarnate stack up in a meta ruled by the mighty Mega Rayquaza and filled with several Mega Evolutions? Let’s go over this Legendary’s stats and movepool, and then gauge its standing in the Flying department.

Did you see the DPSxDPE figure of Bleakwind Storm? It’s literally more than double what Hurricane brings to the table. Well, things are looking bleak (no pun intended) for Shadow Tornadus Incarnate. As such, Shadow Tornadus Incarnate does deserve a round of applause for that. 

That said, Shadow Tornadus Incarnate’s glory is short-lived. When you look at the bigger picture and take a look at how this Pokémon fares against the rest of the meta, it is a tad disappointing. Shadow Tornadus Incarnate is a Tier 5 Shadow Raid Boss. It’s a pure Flying type Pokémon, making it weak to Ice Electric and Rock type attacks.

It can be shiny!

Shadow Tornadus Incarnate can be caught with the following Combat Power values:

  • From 1762 CP to 1911 CP, with no weather boost
  • From 2203 CP to 2389 CP with Windy weather boost

You will need to be well prepared with top counters, correct moveset, powered-up Pokémon, and most importantly, Purified Gems. We would recommend a minimum of 4-6 trainers for Shadow Tornadus Incarnate (and using Purified Gems).

Tips and Tricks

Communication will be key for this raid! You will want to plan not only your Mega Pokémon team positions and counters, but also your use of Purified Gems, so be sure you communicate with your fellow trainers.

We would suggest groups of 5+ for trainers with top counters that are maxed out and armed with Purified Gems, or 8-10+ for lower-level trainers and those without ideal counters. Purified Gems are a must!

While Shadow Pokémon are extremely expensive to power up, we have included the top Shadow Pokémon you can use against Shadow Landorus Incarnate. Ensure you no longer have Frustration on these Pokémon before considering adding them to your team. If you have any of these as an option, while they may take more damage than non-Shadow Pokémon, they will also deal more.

We would highly recommend the use of Mega Evolved Pokémon in Shadow Landorus raids. They provide not only greater damage output, but also boost Pokémon of the same typing in the raid. We would suggest discussing your counter choices with your fellow trainers and planning Mega Pokémon and their positions in your team accordingly.

If you have a group of 6, for example, one person should have their Mega in slot 1, the next slot 2, the next slot 3, etc., you can try to keep the Mega boost going throughout the raid.

You can also make use of the Party Power raid bonus through Party Play! Party Power is a Raid bonus that fills up as members of your Party attack the Raid Boss. Once the Party Power bonus is full, your next Charge Attack will receive a special boost. You can see the Party Power button and your progress towards achieving the bonus in the bottom left corner of your Raid Battle.

Related reading

  • Pokémon GO Shadow Raids: Comprehensive Guide is an overall guide to all things Shadow Raids

Shadow Raid Information & Advice

As a Shadow Raid, Landorus will hit harder than ever before, so make sure your counters are powered up, have the right moveset, and aren’t weak to the Raid Boss’ moves. These Tier 5 raids are extremely difficult, even for the most prepared trainers, and you will need Purified Gems to defeat them. Shadow Raid Bosses will grow enraged as you battle them, boosting their attack and defense.

You will need to subdue Shadow Landorus using Purified Gems, a new item that can be assembled from Shadow Shards.

Shadow Shards are mysterious gem pieces that may be dropped by Team GO Rocket grunts, leaders, and from Shadow Raids. You will need to gather enough shards to use Professor Willow’s newly invented Shard Refiner, and in return, you’ll be rewarded with a Purified Gem. Be sure to have collected as many as you can before you attempt a Shadow Landorus Raid, as without them, you won’t be able to return it to its normal, non-enraged state.

There are multiple ways Purified Gems can assist your battle against enraged Shadow Raid Bosses:

  • When you use a Purified Gem during a Shadow Raid, the enraged Shadow Raid Boss’s attack and defence will be lowered temporarily. This can give you the opening you need to take them down.
  • You and your fellow Trainers can use more than one Purified Gem during a Shadow Raid. If used at the same time, their effects will stack.
  • If enough Purified Gems are used, the enraged Shadow Raid Boss will be subdued—returned to its non-enraged state—which might give you the edge you need to defeat it!

Purified Gems will show in the bottom left corner of the raid battle when you can use them, so be sure to communicate with your raid group to stack their effects!

Good luck, trainers!

item.content:encoded:
Pokémon GO has revealed a fresh batch of details for GO Wild Area 2026, including the ability to show Pokémon backgrounds on Trainer profiles (yes!!!), private Dynamax Battle groups, new Special Research bonuses, and several avatar items.

The updates arrive just ahead of GO Wild Area: Mexico City and GO Wild Area: Sendai, which take place from November 6–8, 2026. The adventure continues worldwide with GO Wild Area: Global on November 14–15, 2026.

Here is everything new that Trainers should know before the event begins.

What’s new for GO Wild Area 2026?

  • Location Backgrounds and Special Backgrounds can now appear on Trainer profiles
  • Private groups are coming to Dynamax Battles
  • Steel Scholar and Dragon Defender medals unlock special Mighty Pokémon catch bonuses
  • New GO Pass rewards, avatar items, and an exclusive pose
  • Pokémon caught in GO Safari Balls can now be transferred to Pokémon HOME
  • Select Adventure Effects can be activated directly from Raid and Max Battle lobbies

Pokémon Backgrounds Are Coming to Trainer Profiles

Starting with GO Wild Area 2026, Trainers will be able to display their Buddy Pokémon’s Location Background or Special Background on their Trainer profile. These backgrounds will also be visible to friends, giving Trainers a new way to show off Pokémon caught during special events and memorable adventures.

The feature will roll out in stages:

  • November 6, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. local time – Sendai and Mexico City GO Wild Area 2026 Location Backgrounds become available to display
  • November 9, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. local time – The GO Wild Area 2026 Special Background and all previously released Location Backgrounds become available to display

Additional Special Backgrounds will be supported in the future.

Important

The feature unlocks according to each Trainer’s local time. Friends will not be able to see your Buddy Pokémon’s background until the feature has reached its scheduled unlock time in their own time zone.

Private Dynamax Battles Are Finally Here

One of the biggest gameplay improvements arriving with GO Wild Area is the ability to join Dynamax Battles privately.

Previously, entering a Max Battle lobby would automatically match Trainers with other participants. Starting with GO Wild Area 2026, Trainers will have two options when joining a battle:

  • Battle: Automatically match with other players in the lobby
  • Private Group: Enter a group code to join an existing private Max Battle group

This should make it easier for coordinated groups to tackle difficult Max Battles without being automatically matched with other players.

The change arrives just in time for Gigantamax Duraludon, Dynamax Dialga, and Dynamax Palkia, all of which are featured during GO Wild Area 2026.

For more information about their appearances, check out our GO Wild Area 2026: Global guide.

Steel Scholar and Dragon Defender Medal Bonuses

Ticket-holding Trainers participating in GO Wild Area: Global will receive a branching Special Research story starting on November 14, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. local time.

Trainers must choose between researching Steel-type or Dragon-type Pokémon. Each path awards a corresponding in-game medal and unlocks special bonuses for catching mighty Pokémon of that type.

Steel Scholar Medal

Trainers who earn the Steel Scholar medal will unlock:

  • 1 additional Candy XL when catching Steel-type mighty Pokémon (Trainer level 31+)
  • 1,000 additional Stardust when catching Steel-type mighty Pokémon

Dragon Defender Medal

Trainers who earn the Dragon Defender medal will unlock:

  • 1 additional Candy XL when catching Dragon-type mighty Pokémon (Trainer level 31+)
  • 1,000 additional Stardust when catching Dragon-type mighty Pokémon

The bonuses activate after claiming the corresponding medal, rather than immediately upon choosing a Research path.

Both sets of bonuses expire when GO Wild Area: Global ends on November 15, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. local time.

Unlike Global participants, ticket-holding Trainers attending Sendai or Mexico City will have the opportunity to earn both medals through their in-person event Special Research, unlocking both sets of bonuses until the conclusion of the Global event.

New GO Wild Area 2026 Avatar Items and Pose

Several new avatar customization options have been revealed, including free GO Pass rewards, paid items, and a Special Research reward.

GO Pass: Into the Wild Rewards

The following items will be available through GO Pass: Into the Wild:

  • GO Wild Area 2026 Tee (Purple) as a Free GO Pass reward
  • Duraludon Pants as a Paid GO Pass Deluxe reward

GO Pass: Into the Wild runs from November 9 at 10:00 a.m. until November 15 at 6:00 p.m. local time.

Trainers have until November 17, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. local time to claim their unlocked rewards.

New In-Game Shop Items

Three additional avatar items will be available for purchase during the event:

  • Duraludon Helmet
  • Gigantamax Duraludon Backpack
  • Fighting-Type Jacket

These items will remain available in the in-game shop after GO Wild Area concludes.

GO Wild Area 2026 Avatar Pose

Ticket-holding Trainers who complete their event Special Research during the in-person GO Wild Area events or GO Wild Area: Global will receive an exclusive new avatar pose.

GO Safari Ball Pokémon Can Now Be Transferred to Pokémon HOME

There is also good news for collectors!

Pokémon caught using GO Safari Balls can now be transferred from Pokémon GO to Pokémon HOME.

Once transferred, their GO Safari Ball will appear as a Strange Ball in Pokémon HOME.

This means Pokémon caught during GO Wild Area using these special Poké Balls are no longer excluded from Pokémon HOME transfers simply because of the Ball they were caught in.

Adventure Effects Can Be Activated in Battle Lobbies

Starting with the Into the Wild event, Trainers will be able to activate select Adventure Effects while waiting in a Raid or Max Battle lobby.

This includes Adventure Effects associated with:

  • Crowned Sword Zacian's Behemoth Blade
  • Crowned Shield Zamazenta's Behemoth Bash

Instead of activating an Adventure Effect before joining a lobby, Trainers can prepare their bonuses while assembling their battle group.

Ticket-holding Trainers attending the in-person GO Wild Area events in Sendai and Mexico City will receive early access to this functionality.

GO Wild Area 2026 Event Maps and Add-Ons

Trainers attending the in-person events can now preview the official event maps to help plan their routes, stops, and activities. The maps and location information are available on the official event pages:

  • Sendai • Tohoku — Official event map and in-person experiences
  • Mexico City — Official event information and in-person experiences

Official event pages: Sendai • Tohoku | Mexico City

Additional event ticket add-ons are also still available for eligible attendees. These provide various gameplay bonuses, additional gameplay days, and merchandise preorder options.

Ticket add-on bonuses are active from November 6 through November 8, 2026, allowing eligible Trainers to benefit throughout the in-person event weekend.

For full event schedules, featured Pokémon, ticket details, and bonuses, check out our comprehensive guides:

  • Pokémon GO Wild Area 2026: Sendai • Tohoku
  • Pokémon GO Wild Area 2026: Mexico City

item.content:encoded:
The Explorer Gadget is getting a useful upgrade in Pokémon GO! Trainers can now use it to automatically catch Pokémon and spin PokéStops while actively playing the game, rather than only when Pokémon GO is running in the background.

Alongside the Explorer Gadget improvements, several quality-of-life updates have recently rolled out, including a redesigned catch summary, a dedicated Appraise button, clearer PokéStop visuals, and changes to Power Spot encounters.

Here’s what’s new and how it works.

Explorer Gadget Now Works While Playing Pokémon GO

Previously, the Explorer Gadget could automatically attempt to catch Pokémon and spin PokéStops while Pokémon GO wasn’t actively open on your device. With this update, it can now do both while you’re playing, much like a Pokémon GO Plus + accessory.

Trainers level 20 and above can activate the Explorer Gadget by tapping its icon in the top-right corner of the Map View or finding it under Key Items in the Item Bag.

When active, a pink Poké Ball icon will appear above Pokémon or PokéStops that the Explorer Gadget is attempting to interact with.

Manual Catching and Spinning Still Work

You can still catch Pokémon or spin PokéStops yourself while the Explorer Gadget is active.

Simply tap the Pokémon or PokéStop that the Gadget is targeting to take over the interaction. However, you’ll only have a limited window of time to do so once the pink Poké Ball icon appears.

Explorer Gadget Limitations

There are a few important restrictions to keep in mind:

  • The Explorer Gadget will not attempt to catch certain Pokémon, including Pokémon not yet registered in your Pokédex and mighty Pokémon.
  • You can keep your Pokémon GO Plus + or other accessory paired, but the Explorer Gadget and an accessory cannot be active simultaneously.
  • You have only a short window to manually override an Explorer Gadget interaction.

Check Your Explorer Gadget Activity

Trainers can review which Pokémon the Explorer Gadget caught and how many PokéStops it spun by opening the Explorer Gadget from the Map View or the Key Items section of the Item Bag.

If you’re unfamiliar with this feature, check out our Explorer Gadget guide for more information.

Other Quality-of-Life Updates

The Explorer Gadget isn’t the only thing getting attention. Pokémon GO has also rolled out several smaller gameplay and interface improvements.

Improved Catch Summary

The screen displayed after catching a Pokémon has been redesigned, with clearer visuals for catch rewards and bonuses. This should make it easier to see exactly what you earned from each catch.

Dedicated Appraise Button

Checking a Pokémon’s IVs is now easier! A dedicated Appraise button has been added to Pokémon summary screens, just above the Additional Options button.

This removes the need to open the Additional Options menu every time you want to appraise a Pokémon.

Changes to Power Spot Encounters

Visiting a Power Spot or placing a Pokémon at a Power Spot after winning a Max Battle will no longer trigger special wild encounters around the Power Spot.

According to Pokémon GO, this change is intended to improve the consistency of wild encounters for all players.

Updated Encounter Rings

The visual rings surrounding wild Pokémon attracted by Lure Modules or encountered while exploring Routes have been updated.

Clearer PokéStop Colors

Spun PokéStops now have adjusted color saturation, making them easier to distinguish from unspun PokéStops.

This is a welcome accessibility improvement, particularly for Trainers who have difficulty distinguishing between similar colors.

Updated Mystery Box and Coin Bag Effects

The visual effects surrounding Pokémon attracted by the Mystery Box or Coin Bag have also been refreshed.

These are relatively small changes individually, but together they should make everyday Pokémon GO gameplay a little more convenient.

Bountiful Banquet Week Vol. 1 is coming in Pokémon Sleep, with a focus on ingredient focused Pokémon and bringing with it the debut of Cottonee and Whimsicott!

Meal Prep Week Vol. 1

Bonuses

The following bonuses will occur on all days of the event:

  • Certain Pokémon will be more likely to appear during sleep research.
  • A few Pokémon of different sleep types will appear during sleep research regardless of your sleep type for that day.
  • During the event, Snorlax’s requested dishes will be set to “Anything!”, allowing you to make any dish.
  • Each time a helper Pokémon with the Ingredients specialty brings you ingredients as it usually would, it will have 1 extra, and it will also bring an additional Snackable Nuts ×1.
  • The maximum number of Berries and ingredients that helper Pokémon with the Ingredients specialty can carry will be increased by 10.
  • Strength gains from the required ingredients will be multiplied by 1.5 when a dish whose recipe includes Snackable Nuts is made.
  • Strength gains will be multiplied by 1.5 for each Snackable Nuts used outside of a dish’s required ingredients.
  • Your cooking pot will be able to fit 30 extra ingredients

The following bonuses will be available for dishes made with Snackable Nuts:

  • The multiplier applied to the Strength gained from dishes that include Snackable Nuts will change depending on the dish made and the number of Snackable Nuts used.

Example 1: Creating a dish that includes Snackable Nuts as a required ingredient, and only using the required amount of Snackable Nuts. The Strength gained from the dish, as displayed in the recipe list, will be multiplied by 1.5.

Example 2: Creating a dish that includes Snackable Nuts as a required ingredient, and using more than the required amount of Snackable Nuts. The Strength gained from the dish, as displayed in the recipe list, will be multiplied by 1.5. The Strength gained from each additional Snackable Nuts used over the required amount will be multiplied by 1.5.

Example 3: Using Snackable Nuts in a dish that does not include Snackable Nuts as a required ingredient. The Strength gained from the dish, as displayed in the recipe list, will remain unchanged. The Strength gained from each additional Snackable Nuts used will be multiplied by 1.5.

Cottonee and Whimsicott Debut

Starting November 16th, 2026, at 3:00 p.m. Cottonee and Whimsicott will make their Pokémon Sleep debut! They will both be Fairy types, with a Snoozing Sleep Style.

They will appear at Greengrass Isle, Cyan Beach, Amber Canyon, Greengrass Isle (Expert), and Cyan Beach (Expert).

  • Event bonuses do not apply to sleep tracking during the tutorial.
  • If overlapping events trigger more than one of the same type of bonus, the larger bonus will be applied.

With Shadow and Mega forms push that reputation even further, Mega Gengar sits just behind the newly introduced Mega Chandelure among Ghost attackers. Since Gengar is appearing in the wild during the event, this is an excellent opportunity to grind for its XL Candies. Gigantamax Gengar is also a great addition to your Dynamax battle squads, and you’ll need Candy and XL Candy to optimise it too.

Litwick and Shuppet are also excellent targets for Trainers building out their Ghost raid rosters. Mega Chandelure’s Super Mega Raid Day has just concluded, making this an ideal window to collect any missing Litwick Candy or XL Candy. Shadow Chandelure ranks among the very best Ghost type raid attackers in the game, while Mega Chandelure goes a step further and currently stands as the very best Ghost attacker in the game. Mega Banette is a respectable alternative, though it trails both Mega Chandelure and Mega Gengar. It remains a useful stopgap for Trainers who have not yet built either of those Mega Evolutions.

Well, not every spooky addition is a PvE winner. Mega Sableye, despite receiving Night Shade+, does not make a meaningful impact in raids and remains primarily a PvP-oriented pick. Thanks to a strong 248 Attack stat and a serviceable moveset, it performs decently as a Ghost attacker and can serve as a backup option. However, its accessibility is limited because Sinistea is only available through raids, which makes building Polteageist less practical.

Starter Costumes: Rowlet & Froakie

Beyond the Ghost types, two costumed first-partner Pokémon are featured in the wild, Rowlet and Froakie. Both can evolve into their final forms, Decidueye and Greninja respectively, making them worth a closer look.

Decidueye does not impress as a Ghost attacker, but it performs somewhat better as a Grass attacker thanks to Frenzy Plant. Even so, it falls outside the Top 20 Grass Attackers, which is an underwhelming result for a Grass type starter. Unless you are collecting costumes or completing your Pokédex, Rowlet is not a high-priority PvE investment.

Parting Words

Halloween 2026 may be themed around ghosts and ghouls, but the real treats this time are the raid-ready Pokémon hiding among the spooky spawns. Whether you are chasing XL Candy for Mega Gengar, completing your Chandelure line-up or farming Froakie for a top-tier Mega Greninja, there is plenty here to justify a few extra walks before the event ends.

If your resources are limited, prioritize in this order:

  • Froakie — for Mega Greninja’s dual Water and Dark type performance.
  • Litwick — to complete or strengthen Mega and Shadow Chandelure.
  • Gengar — for XL Candy and future-proofing Mega Gengar and Gigantamax Gengar.

Tips and Tricks

Communication will be key for this raid! Plan not only your Mega Pokémon team positions and counters, but also your use of Purified Gems, and communicate with your fellow trainers.

We suggest groups of 2-3+ for trainers with maxed-out top counters and Purified Gems, or 5-6+ for lower-level trainers and those without ideal counters. Purified Gems are a must!

While Shadow Pokémon are extremely expensive to power up, we have included the top Shadow Pokémon you can use against Shadow Poliwhirl. Ensure you no longer have Frustration on these Pokémon before considering adding them to your team. If you have any of these as an option, while they may take more damage than non-Shadow Pokémon, they will also deal more.

We would highly recommend the use of Mega Evolved Pokémon in Shadow Poliwhirl raids. They provide not only greater damage output, but also boost Pokémon of the same typing in the raid. We would suggest discussing your counter choices with your fellow trainers and planning Mega Pokémon and their positions in your team accordingly.

If you have a group of 6, for example, one person should have their Mega in slot 1, the next slot 2, the next slot 3, etc., you can try to keep the Mega boost going throughout the raid.

You can also make use of the Party Power raid bonus through Party Play! Party Power is a Raid bonus that fills up as members of your Party attack the Raid Boss. Once the Party Power bonus is full, your next Charge Attack will receive a special boost. You can see the Party Power button and your progress towards achieving the bonus in the bottom left corner of your Raid Battle.

Related reading

  • Pokémon GO Shadow Raids: Comprehensive Guide is an overall guide to all things Shadow Raids

Shadow Raid Information & Advice

As a Shadow Raid, Poliwhirl will hit harder than ever before, so make sure your counters are powered up, have the right moveset, and aren’t weak to the Raid Boss’ moves. These Tier 3 raids are quite difficult, even for the most prepared trainers, and you will need Purified Gems to defeat them. Shadow Raid Bosses will grow enraged as you battle them, boosting their attack and defense.

You will need to subdue Shadow Poliwhirl using Purified Gems, an item that can be assembled from Shadow Shards.

Shadow Shards are mysterious gem pieces that may be dropped by Team GO Rocket grunts, leaders, and from Shadow Raids. You will need to gather enough shards to use Professor Willow’s newly invented Shard Refiner, and in return, you’ll be rewarded with a Purified Gem. Be sure to have collected as many as you can before you attempt a Shadow Prinplup Raid, as without them, you won’t be able to return it to its normal, non-enraged state.

There are multiple ways Purified Gems can assist your battle against enraged Shadow Raid Bosses:

  • When you use a Purified Gem during a Shadow Raid, the enraged Shadow Raid Boss’s attack and defence will be lowered temporarily. This can give you the opening you need to take them down.
  • You and your fellow Trainers can use more than one Purified Gem during a Shadow Raid. If used at the same time, their effects will stack.
  • If enough Purified Gems are used, the enraged Shadow Raid Boss will be subdued—returned to its non-enraged state—which might give you the edge you need to defeat it!

Purified Gems will show in the bottom left corner of the raid battle when you can use them, so be sure to communicate with your raid group to stack their effects!

Good luck, trainers!

The week of November 2–8, 2026 wraps up spooky season with Halloween Part Two, the start of November’s GO Pass, and two in-person GO Wild Area events. Altered Forme Giratina replaces Origin Forme Giratina in five-star raids on Wednesday, November 4, while Mega Sableye continues in Mega Raids. Dynamax Machop headlines Max Monday, and Halloween Teddiursa takes the Spotlight Hour stage with 2× Evolution XP. Here’s the full schedule, including events, Raid Hour, Spotlight Hour, Max Battles, GO Battle League rotations and seasonal bonuses.

Quick Summary

  • Monday, November 2 – Dynamax Machop Max Monday runs from 6:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. local time.
  • Tuesday, November 3 – GO Pass: November begins at 10:00 a.m. local time, featuring Groudon and PokéCoin rewards.
  • Tuesday, November 3 – GO Battle League rotates at 1:00 p.m. PST (9:00 p.m. UTC) to Great League: Mega Edition, Ultra League: Mega Edition, and Master League: Mega Edition, with 4× Stardust from win rewards (excluding end-of-set rewards).
  • Wednesday, November 4 – Altered Forme Giratina enters five-star raids and Shadow Incarnate Forme Tornadus begins its new Shadow Raid rotation at 6:00 a.m. local time. Altered Forme Giratina is featured in Raid Hour from 6:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. local time.
  • Thursday, November 5 – Halloween Teddiursa Spotlight Hour runs from 6:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. local time with 2× Evolution XP.
  • Thursday, November 5 – Halloween Part Two and the Halloween GO Pass end at 8:00 p.m. local time.
  • Friday, November 6 – GO Wild Area: Mexico City and GO Wild Area: Sendai • Tohoku begin at 10:00 a.m. local time in their respective host cities. Both run through Sunday, November 8.

Events in Pokémon GO This Week

GO Pass: Halloween 2026

The Halloween 2026 GO Pass began on October 27 at 10:00 a.m. local time and ends on November 5 at 8:00 p.m. local time. Trainers can also raise Mega Sableye to Super Max Level, unlocking access to the additional Charged Attack Night Shade+ while Mega Evolved.

Wild Area Sendai • Tohoku

GO Wild Area 2026: Sendai • Tohoku runs from November 6–8, 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. JST each day, with Steel- and Dragon-themed gameplay in Sendai and the surrounding Miyagi Prefecture, Japan. Dynamax Dialga, Dynamax Palkia, and Gigantamax Duraludon make their Pokémon GO debuts, mighty Pokémon return, and a new costumed Machamp appears. This is a ticketed, in-person event. 

Wild Area Mexico City

GO Wild Area 2026: Mexico City takes place on November 6–8, from 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. local time each day, with gameplay throughout the Mexico City metropolitan area. Gigantamax Duraludon debuts in six-star Max Battles, while Dynamax Dialga and Dynamax Palkia also make their Pokémon GO debuts. Steel- and Dragon-type Pokémon take the spotlight, Hisuian Sliggoo and Hisuian Goodra debut, and a new costumed Machamp appears.
