Pokémon TCG Pocket has dropped several incredible cards in its Dual Fusion major expansion (C1 set). Featuring jaw-dropping artwork and powerful ex cards as well as regular cards, you must be wondering how the Trainers in this set perform in the meta.

Well, you’ll find the answers to all your questions about the new Trainer cards in Dual Fusion, and trust me, you’ll also be surprised how insanely powerful some of them are! Let’s dig in.

Items

Sweet Honey

Mayday! Mayday! We have a new Lucky Ice Pop, and it’s an Item, so you can use them together. Indeed, dear reader… Sweet Honey is sweet vengeance when your opponent dares to damage your Pokémon. Flip a coin until you get tails, and for each head, you heal 20 DMG from the recipient!

We all know how infuriating it is when you see your opponent healing multiple instances of 20 DMG using the Lucky Ice Pop. Well, now we literally add “Sweet Honey” to the Pop. You can bet this would be one of the most used Items in current and future metas. This Item is so special that it got an Illustration Rare card in this set!

Super Potion

The healing shenanigans in the Dual Fusion set don’t end with Sweet Honey, as we have another Item called Super Potion that heals a whopping 40 DMG, but at the cost of a random Energy. Now, that discarded Energy doesn’t matter usually, since you can simply replace it on the next turn. This is a great card to use in Mega Charizard Y decks, as this Zard takes 50 recoil damage on unleashing its monstrous 250 DMG attack. In fact, this can be used in tandem with Pokémon Center Lady to heal damage on multiple instances if the first victim isn’t a Mega Evolution or tanks Mega Zard Y. Super Potion can also replace the Lady if you want to reserve the deck slot for another card.

However, Super Potion shouldn’t be used on Mega Sceptile ex, Mega Blaziken ex, or Dragon Pokémon using multiple Energy types. Even in cases wherein you need to use more than one attacker, Super Potion can make things tricky for you. This is a fantastic healing Item for specific decks, so pick it wisely.

Full Heal

What are we doing, TCG Pocket? Another healing Item in Dual Fusion?! Alright, alright, we are healing Special Conditions with Full Heal, but still! Jokes aside, Special Conditions can be brutal and often spell endgame for you. If you don’t have space in your deck for Teal Mask Ogerpon ex, this can be used to save the Active Pokémon from those pesky situations. Sure, you can use both Lucky Ice Pop/Sweet Honey/Super Potion and Full Heal, but keep in mind that Pokémon Center Lady is a middle ground that saves deck space. 

We now have plenty of Trainers that offer healing support to your mons, so it’s all about creating decks smartly and thinking through which cards suit your deck slots better.

Max Repel

Phew! Finally, we have a non-healing Item in Dual Fusion. The Max Repel Item comes with niche usage against Stage 2 opponents, where you want to switch them out. This tech often goes in vain if your opponent is simply able to retreat the new Active Pokémon (which they choose, lol) and bring back their Stage 2 attacker to destroy you. Max Repel is also useless if your opponent is running a deck full of Basics and/or Stage 1 mons. As such, it brings real value only if you’re able to KO the incoming Pokémon after the Stage 2 is switched out.

Arguably the weakest Item from this set, and it’s the one that doesn’t heal.  

Pokémon Tools

Pokémon Tools are super useful cards that have been available in the physical TCG games and follow these rules in Pokémon TCG Pocket:

  • Pokémon Tool cards can be attached to your Active or Benched cards, and they provide some special battle effects.
  • They stay attached to the Pokémon in question until it leaves play.
  • Like Item cards, you can use as many Pokémon Tool cards as you like during a turn, but each Pokémon can have only one Tool attached at a time.

Light Ball

Light Tool is a custom-built Tool for Pikachu ex, and specifically the Pika from Dual Fusion, since this combination is one of the most devastating forces in Pokémon TCG Pocket.

With Light Ball, Pikachu ex dishes out a jaw-dropping 60 DMG for only 1 Energy, easily OHKOing Babies like Igglybuff, Basics like Charmander, and cripple higher HP opponents. Gathering 3 Energy for Pikachu ex is no big deal, as it gets that assistance from Magneton, the new Pawmot, and Elemental Switch, but when it does, Light Ball takes the damage output to 160 DMG. This is no doubt the best tailor-made item for any Pokémon in TCG Pocket, making Pikachu ex decks the fastest as well.

Eviolite

Basic Pokémon are always trending in TCG Pocket, and the Dual Fusion set itself brings some bangers in this category, including Mega Mewtwo X ex, Mew ex, Giratina ex, and Fuecoco ex. With Eviolite, these powerhouses can brush off 20 DMG from the opponent, which is crucial when you’re setting up your battle formation. With a slew of healing support in tow, your Basic can remain in pristine health when it’s finally all set to attack or is done with its job of stalling, but is still healthy enough to not get sniped by the likes of Water Shuriken Greninja.

Supporters

Lorelei

The Dual Fusion set is chock full of strong ex cards, but it also has some spicy picks. Or should I say “icy spicy” picks, since these originally Ice-type Pokémon (Water in TCG Pocket) distribute high damage output amongst your battlefield courtesy of Lorelei, the Ice-type specialist from the Kanto Region and a member of the Elite Four.

 

Each of these attackers deals surprise damage to 1 or more of the opponent’s Pokémon, and Lorelei boosts that damage. Of course, the final damage output isn’t high enough to directly score KOs, but they can surely weaken opponents to a great degree. These are some fun cards for sure, they’re decently functional, and they put some serious dents in the opposition’s armor, making it easy for your ex to finish the job.

Blue’s Provocation

Blue’s Provocation rings in true Kanto nostalgia as the powerful Supporter powers up four of the most iconic Gen 1 stars: Venusaur, Charizard, Blastoise, and Pidgeot by switching in a chosen Pokémon from your Bench to the Active Spot, as long as these are in play. Let’s talk about each.

Venusaur

With Venusaur on the Bench, you not only heal 30 DMG from your Active hitter, but also help bring the target to the forefront. This is an excellent addition to the bulky Mega Venusaur ex deck, which also poisons the target and puts it to sleep. Maybe have a Darkrai in handy for some extra chip damage on the asleep Pokémon.

That said, keep in mind that Pokémon and Trainer cards are widely available to keep Special Conditions like Poison and Sleep at bay. So while this deck is strong, it may not go according to plan.

Charizard

No surprise that Charizard is not only the strongest among Blue’s Provocation recipients, but also among the top Pokémon from the Dual Fusion set. For each Energy you attach to Zard, you deal 30 chip damage to the opponent’s Active card. And Zard can achieve this while being comfortably seated on the Bench.

In fact, Dual Fusion Charizard is a perfect addition to Mega Charizard Y decks, where this Zard can eliminate Oricorio and put more pressure on an opponent that is already dreading the 250 DMG hit from Mega Charizard Y. It also adds to the damage numbers on the opponent to assist Mega Charizard X, whose firepower at more than half of its HP is relatively low. For these reasons, Dual Fusion Charizard fits like a glove in the infamous Mega Charizard X and Y combo deck, destroying Oricorio and making the setup more intimidating. You can also skip Mega Zard X to include Fuecoco ex into the Zard | Mega Zard Y entourage. In any case, having this powerful Zard in play lets Blue’s Provocation summon a sitting duck for Mega Zard Y to annihilate (ideally a Mega Evolution).

Blastoise

Blastoise is often neglected among the Kanto starters, and the Dual Fusion set is no different, with Blastoise being the worst among the trio. Yes, Blue still drags a Benched Pokémon of your choice, letting you attack the poor, unprepared target, but it’s the ability that is super underwhelming compared to Venu and Zard.

While Venu heals and Zard sends some great chip damage, Blasty Boi/Gurl takes a Energy from the Energy Zone and attaches it to… itself! But why, my good ‘Toise? You dish out a meager 100 DMG for 3 Energy; what are you actually doing against those 200+ HP Mega Evolutions? No wonder Blastoise is categorized as the ‘Shellfish’ Pokémon.  

Pidgeot

Finally, we have the regional Bird, Pidgeot. Give some respect to its name, as Pidgeot does a clean 100 DMG for only 1 Colorless Energy! This is extremely Energy-efficient and can boost the power of any team, given its Colorless typing. Pidgeot surpasses Blastoise convincingly, and can be tied with Venusaur for utility. Props to this underrated Pokémon as it spices up any deck in TCG Pocket!

Serena’s Choice

Serena’s Choice is a valuable addition to any deck, increasing your drawing power and often helping you find your desired card more quickly. This immediately begs the question of whether it should replace Professor’s Research or Copycat, and the answer is neither. Serena’s Choice literally gives you the choice to pick the most useful card from the top 3 cards of your deck, but its drawing power is still lower than both Professor’s Research and Copycat. It should ideally be used in turns not involving those two (or when Copycat is not feasible).

This Supporter definitely deserves a place in your deck, and in those wherein you use 2 copies of the Professor or Copycat, feel free to replace 1 copy with Serena.

Rika

If you thought Lorelei was strong, meet Rika from Paldea’s Elite Four. She (yes, Rika is a woman) grants 2x Energy to 1 of your Whiscash or Paldean Clodsire, two Energy-hungry Pokémon.

Whiscash initially deals only 40 DMG for 1x Energy, which is neat. But if it gains 3 more of that Energy, it deals a shocking 100 DMG! Thanks to Rika, you can manage this in just two turns, with 2 of those Energies coming from successive turns and 2 from Rika.

Now, coming to Paldean Clodsire (Rika’s signature Pokémon), you get an actually strong non-ex mon that is almost as vicious as Hydreigon. Ready in just 2 turns courtesy of Rika, Paldean Clodsire shells out 130 DMG and also sneaks in 20 DMG to each of the opponent’s Benched cards! This is some serious damage output, and establishes Paldean Clodsire as a legit match winner. 

Note that both Whiscash and Paldean Clodsire are Stage 1, so their HP can be increased by +30  via the Elegant Cape Tool (Whiscash gets 150 HP and Paldean Clodsire gets 160 HP). Rika is definitely meta!

Poké Mart Guy

If you have successfully managed to build a deck focused on healing and included multiple copies of Super Potion, Max Repel, or Full Heal, the Poké Mart Guy brings any random 2 copies of those. If you include, say, 1x Full Heal and 1x Max Potion, using this Supporter is guaranteed to bring both. To be fair, a deck with so many slots being occupied with these is a bit tough to run, especially when many of your opponents are bulky, hard-hitting Megas. Again, this one’s for the spice.

Rising Star

The Rising Star Supporter provides free retreat, no matter what the retreat cost is. The only limitation is that the deck it’s used in should contain at least 3 different Pokémon types in play. Sounds daunting, but there are some great examples of this archetype:

  • Sleep Scam decks consisting of Igglybuff (Colorless), Darkrai (Darkness), and any other type, say Mega Lucario ex (Fighting) or Mega Sharpedo ex/Milotic ex (Water).
  • Any deck led by a Dual type such as Mega Mewtwo X ex (Psychic/Fighting) or Mega Greninja ex (Water/Darkness) and joined by a Colorless type or something like Teal Mask Ogerpon ex (Grass type; used for immunity to Special Attacks) or Oricorio (Lightning type; immunity to attacks from ex Pokémon). 

Rising Star decks are usually strategy-oriented, so expect to see it in Ranked battles. This is the dark horse of the Dual Fusion set.

Stadium Cards

Stadiums are Trainer cards whose effects affect all Pokémon in play (both you and your opponent) and can be used once per turn.

  • This card stays in play after you use it, unlike Items and Supporters, which are discarded after they are used.
  • Only one Stadium can be in play at a time, and you discard it only when a new Stadium enters the battlefield, or a Pokémon/Trainer effect disposes of it.
  • You can’t play Stadium cards with the same name while that Stadium is already active.

Abandoned Station

We have a new Stadium card with coin flip shenanigans, and it’s the Abandoned Station, which lets you draw a card if you obtain heads. Definitely a useful card when you get heads more often, and complements decks consisting of Suicune ex or Entei ex pretty well, whether to fill up the Bench in the former or quickly pull the entire Charizard line in the latter. 

 

The Trainer cards from Dual Fusion don’t disappoint, as most of them are excellent additions to the ever-evolving TCG Pocket meta, complementing the strong Pokémon Pokémon from this set. 

Happy collecting and battling!

item.content:encoded:
The Pokémon TCG Pocket meta has undergone a continental shift with the arrival of the first booster pack of the C series: the Dual Fusion major expansion (C1 set). Featuring the new Dual types, Mega Evolutions, and several strong cards in the roster, trainers are more excited than ever!

One major reason behind this surge is the new line of ex cards that have caused a tidal wave to hit the meta. So let’s dive into all the Pokémon ex that have erupted in Dual Fusion.

Mega Mewtwo X ex

We begin with one of the two Dual types in this set, and also one of the headliners of Dual Fusion: Mega Mewtwo X ex. First, let’s look at how this Psychic/Fighting-type powerhouse works.

  • Dual typing means that a wider pool of Pokémon are weak to its attacks. As such, Mega Mewtwo X’s attacks will do super-effective damage (+20 DMG) to Pokémon weak to Psychic and Fighting. Therefore, it deals +20 DMG to Fighting types (weak to Psychic) as well as Metal types (weak to Fighting)
  • It can use all Trainer cards whose effects apply to Psychic and Fighting types. So you can use Korrina and Arena of Antiquity to boost its damage, and Peculiar Plaza to reduce its retreat cost by 2 (free for Mega Mewtwo X ex!).

Mega Mewtwo X ex will function like a Basic Mega Lucario ex, with Korrina, Arena of Antiquity, and its own move mechanics contributing to an insane 190 DMG! For energy ramp, the new Mew ex (which we shall soon see in this article) serves as a superb accelerator, using its 1x [psychic-type] Energy to give [psychic-type] Energy to your Benched Pokémon corresponding to the number of heads you obtain from three coin flips. Even two heads will suffice to have Mega Mewtwo X ready to go in the next turn, given that the third Energy for attacking is gained from the new turn’s Energy.

Once Mew ex has done its job, withdraw it directly into your Hand using the Budding Expeditioner Supporter, and bring Mega Mewtwo X to the forefront. It really helps that both Mega Mewtwo X ex and Mew ex are Basic Pokémon, making your army threatening from the get-go.

For more support, have one copy of Comfey on the Bench to brush off any Special Condition trap shenanigans.

And since it’s a Psychic deck after all, why not play min games via Flutter Mane ex, who prevents your opponent from using their Trainers the first time it attacks them

Finally, there’s a new Pokémon Tool that helps Basic Pokémon brush off 20 DMG: Eviolite. With this deck brimming with Basics, feel free to use two copies of Eviolite.

The entire unit is a well-oiled machine, made using only Basics while also being Energy-efficient. This deck led by Mega Mewtwo X ex is arguably the best that Peculiar Plaza has ever felt, letting you move around four different Pokémon, each serving a different purpose. It’s also well-balanced, adding to its usability in battle modes.

Pikachu ex

Ladies and gentlemen, Pikachu ex from Dual Fusion is quite possibly the best Lightning-type Pokémon in TCG Pocket and part of the ultimate ‘fast and furious’ deck in the game’s history. Let me explain.

For just 1x [electric-type] Energy, it deals 30 DMG, instantly deleting Baby Pokémon (hello, Igglybuff). And 130 DMG for 3 Energy. But what’s really special is what Pika ex does with a new Tool created exclusively for the game’s mascot: the Light Ball.

This Tool adds a whopping 30 DMG to all Pikachu ex’s attacks. So, for just 1x Energy, you’re dishing out a massive 60 DMG! This is now even enough to take out the Basics of many Stage 2 ex mons! Now, if you’re worried about discarding 2 Energy after using the 160 DMG (w/ Light Ball) move, let me introduce you to Pawmot from Dual Fusion:

Its ability literally gives a free Energy to the Active Pokémon. So once two Energies are discarded, add the turn’s Energy and the Energy from Pawmot (on the Bench) to instantly replenish Pikachu ex and deliver 160 DMG. You can also add the Genetic Apex Magneton into the mix and use Elemental Switch to serve free Energy to Pikachu ex after Magneton generates it on its own. After Miraidon ex, this is the strongest that the Lightning type has felt in TCG Pocket. On that note, this particular Pikachu is also the closest we have to Ash’s Pikachu from the anime, haha.

Alolan Exeggutor ex

Aside from being a straight-up attacker, Alolan Exeggutor ex is a shot in the arm (paw) for Leafeon ex. The popular Eeveelution takes center stage as the main attacker while also supplying Energy to Exeggcute | Alolan Exeggutor on the Bench. Once Alolan Exeggutor ex is all set, retreat Leafeon (only 1 Energy) and unleash this draconic tree, not only inflicting 100 DMG to the opponent’s Active Pokémon, but also chipping in a generous 50 DMG to a random mon from their Bench.

Enter Cyrus, and it’s lights out more often than not for the opponent. Do add a Teal Mask Ogerpon ex on the Bench to prevent Special Condition oopsies, and add in valuable grassy supporters such as Erika, Leaf Cape, and Quick-Grow Extract. This is a fine Grass-type ex which may not be top-tier meta like Mega Sceptile ex, but is a great addition for sure as it can virtually fit into any Grass deck and bring a lot of value to the table.

Fuecoco ex

Don’t be fooled by looking at Fuecoco ex and thinking, “Eh, it’s just Fuecoco, not Skeledirge lol.” If you did, you’re in for a rude awakening, as this little croc is one of the strongest Fire-type Pokémon ex in TCG Pocket! For starters (no pun intended), it can OHKO Babies like Igglybuff. And while it’s Active, if you make the mistake of doing damage to it, it will do an explosive 120 DMG for only 2x Energy!

That’s not all! During the time Fuecoco ex taunts your opponent to attack, you can build a Charizard (or two) on the Bench! Since Fuecoco ex uses 2 Energy, this is a perfect setup for the Flame Patch Item to set up Mega Charizard X or Y (ideally Y).

Also, the new Charizard in the Dual Fusion set is a lethal addition to Zard decks and complements Fuecoco ex pretty well. For every Energy attached to this Zard, you do 30 DMG to your opponent’s Active Pokémon. Basically, you have Fuecoco ex stationed on the Active Spot, build this Charizard on the Bench (you ideally feed two Energy to Charmeleon), and then switch out Fuecoco to bring this monster. Add the next turn’s Energy to deal +30 DMG, and then attack with 90 DMG, making it a total of 120 DMG. This is more damage than Mega Charizard X ex, which technically does only 100 DMG for 3x [fire-energy] until it reaches half or lower HP (in which case, it hits with 180 DMG).

Another amazing perk is that you can give every turn’s Energy to Charizard after it’s live to:

  • Inflict 30 chip damage every turn
  • Retreat it easily
  • Devote the 2 Energies to Mega Charizard Y ex

While Mega Charizard X and Y ex enjoy deck combinations with several partners, such as Moltres ex and Entei ex, Fuecoco ex might very well be the best to join its ranks.

Mega Greninja ex

On the surface, Mega Greninja ex looks like a stronger Kingdra ex, with 30 more HP and 10 more damage in its attack. But what Kingdra lacks is a Dual typing and a good partner… more specifically, a pre-evolution in the form of Frogadier (Dual Fusion).

On evolution, Frogadier summons another Frogadier and places it directly onto your Bench. In a deck accompanied by Suicune ex, include 2x Froakie and 2x Frogadier along with Mega Greninja ex, Greninja ex, and the infamous Water Shuriken Greninja.

  • Evolve one Froakie into Frogadier, summon another Frogadier. Evolve the first Frogadier into one of the Greninja, say, Mega Greninja ex.
  • Now, evolve the second Frogadier into another Greninja (preferably the Water Shuriken variant).
  • Finally, use Rare Candy to evolve the second Froakie into Greninja ex or another Water Shuriken Greninja.
  • This way, you end up having 3 Greninja variants across the board!

The instant summoning of Fraokie also adds to the damage output of Suicune ex. The best part is that Mega Greninja’s attacks do +20 DMG to Pokémon weak to Water (Fire) as well as Darkness (Grass)! And since it’s bound next turn after Mega Greninja ex hits, two Water Shuriken Greninja on the Bench as well as the next attack from Mega Greninja add up to 140!

While this deck obviously requires some setting up to execute its best potential, Mega Greninja ex is a fantastic inclusion to both the Water and Dark metas.

Mew ex

We spoke about Mew ex right at the beginning of your analysis, where we started with Mega Mewtwo X ex. This Pokémon is a superb Energy ramp for Psychic types, with Mega Mewtwo X ex being the biggest beneficiary of this tech. As mentioned earlier, Mew ex works as a support ex rather than being a strong attacker per se. For any future Psychic types and also past powerhouses like Mega Gardevoir ex, Mew ex is the Energy ramp of choice, although the Gardevoir from Fantastical Parade still holds weight.

Lycanroc ex

After Fuecoco ex, here’s another that you would think twice before doing damage on: Lycanroc ex. On mere damage from a direct hit by the opponent, Lycanroc ex does 30 chip damage, and with 2x Energy, it does 70 DMG with Slashing Claw. As usual, with Fighting Coach Lucario (Space-Time Smackdown), the damage goes to 90 DMG or even 110 DMG (if you decide to stack two of those Lucario on the Bench). And against ex Pokémon, the combination of Korrina and Arena of Antiquity Stadium offers an additional 50 DMG.

To put it into perspective:

  • Slashing Claw + Fighting Coach Lucario = 90 DMG (110 DMG with 2x Lucario)
  • Slashing Claw + Fighting Coach Lucario + Korrina + Arena of Antiquity = 140 DMG (160 DMG with another Lucario)
  • Add +30 DMG if Lycanroc is hit with an attack before its turn. 

The Pulsing Aura set has instilled a new leash of life into Fighting Pokémon in TCG Pocket, and Lycanroc ex is just reaping those benefits. Do note that this won’t be anywhere as good as Mega Lucario ex or even closer to home, Mega Mewtwo X ex, but it’s usable for sure. Pair it with good ol’ Rampardos!

Mega Tyranitar ex

Darkness has always been among the best Pokémon types in TCG Pocket, and the latest to join the entourage is Mega Tyranitar ex, a brute that possesses more raw power than the other Darkness-type ex in this set, Mega Greninja ex.

Now, looking at 4x Energy and the same retreat cost seems daunting at first until you realize that Mega Tyranitar ex took a page right out of Mega Venusaur ex’s book and gave it to its pre-evolution, Pupitar. That’s right, just like the Crimson Blaze Ivysaur, Pupitar is an Energy generator.

Using the 1 Energy move Amass, Pupitar generates 2x Energy for itself. In a Darkness Energy deck, this will result in 1x from the turn and 2x Energy from the move. In the next turn, evolve Pupitar into Mega Tyranitar ex and add that turn’s Energy. 

Tada! You have a Mega Tyranitar ex with 2x and 2x Energy, ready to deal a crazy 180 DMG to the opponent. Of course, you discard the top two cards of your deck, but that much damage output justifies the small sacrifice. Be sure to arm Mega Tyranitar with a Heavy Helmet to take 20 less damage from the opponent’s attacks. Bombirdier helps reduce the retreat cost by 1, and the very economical Mega Absol ex is a great partner. You can also add fellow Pseudo Legendary and one of the most feared non-ex Pokémon in TCG Pocket, Hydreigon, to the mix. Or, you can add the new Umbreon to the Mega Tyranitar line and build a simple yet deadly deck. Honestly, try this one, as Umbreon is arguably the most broken Pokémon in the Dual Fusion set.

Seriously, the Darkness type always gets some amazing cards! Welcome aboard the bandwagon, Mega Tyranitar ex!

Mega Skarmory ex

Just like the Darkness type, the Metal type also consistently gets good cards. However, they are not as vicious and often end up being underused set after set. The Dual Fusion set adds Mega Skarmory ex to the mix, and honestly, it’s just a decent Mega Evolution, given the coin flip shenanigans.

Getting the three Energy is no big deal with Dialga ex and Orthworm out there. Once Mega Skarmory is live, it dishes out 90 DMG, and an extra 50 DMG for every head you get until the coin shows tails. Use it with the Will Supporter card to ensure at least a respectable 140 DMG. Of course, with multiple heads, Mega Skarmory ex can go ballistic and deliver the ceiling of damage numbers. However, as is the case with coin flips, high damage output relying on coin flips is too risky in a meta with 200+ HP opponents. Moreover, Mega Skarmory ex is also weak to Fire types, arguably the consistently heaviest hitters in the game. Don’t be surprised if players forget about Mega Skarmory ex as soon as the next set (C2) drops.

Mega Dragonite ex

Similar to how Pulsing Aura was a boon to Fighting types, Ruler of the Skies gave life to Dragon types with a new Dragonair that grants free Energy to the Active Dragon with its ability, and the Rainbow Cave Stadium to possibly change the type of the incoming Energy (since Dragon-type attacks use multiple Energy types). Joining the fray is Mega Dragonite ex, a powerhouse who hits a random Pokémon of the opponent with a devastating 250 DMG!

Pair Mega Dragonite ex with regular Dragonite from Genetic Apex, and to stall in the Active Spot, go with Goomy (increases the opponent’s Energy requirement for attacks by 1) or the 100 HP, 70 DMG-hitting Drampa from Ruler of the Skies. Dragon decks are incredibly rewarding once the main attacker is live, and 250 DMG from Mega Dragonite ex is no joke. Imagine hitting a Mega Evolution and ending the game in your favor right there!

Giratina ex

The Psychic-type Giratina ex from Shining Revelry (featuring the Altered Forme) was one of the most monumental additions to TCG Pocket, with this Pokémon ruling the Ranked mode for months. And now, we have another Giratina ex, this time featuring the Origin Forme and the Dragon typing.

This Legendary employs the same arrangement as Mega Dragonite ex or any current Dragon, with Dragonair, Rainbow Cave, and Goomy/Drampa in the setup. It can, however, deal 50 DMG with two Colorless Energy, and this, dear reader, is what makes this Giratina ex special. So not only does this Dragon require the least Energy to attack, but it’s also Colorless, meaning any Energy will do. As such, there is less reliance on Rainbow Cave, as any Energy type will do until you get both and Energies. Speaking of the Psychic type, do you realize that you can even pair this Giratina ex with the OG Giratina ex in a Psychic deck?! The latter generates Energy on its own after all!

And if you want to spice up your deck and make ot more versatile to deal with Oricorio, simply add the Space-Time Smackdown Giratina.

With even a single Energy attached, this Giratina has no retreat cost! Also, Eviolite helps Giratina ex sustain itself better in the Active Spot, although an argument can be made for Giant Cape also. Regardless of which Tool you use, Giratina ex is one of the most fun additions to the ever-evolving Dragon meta and can get more prominent as this season’s Ranked battles progress.

Bewear ex

The final ex card in the Dual Fusion set is Bewear ex, a Colorless type and one that also relies on coin flips for high damage. For 3 Energy, this teddy does 100 DMG, and if you flip 2 coins and get heads on both, you scale to 200 DMG. Now, the Will Supporter guarantees 1 head, but there’s no way to ensure that you obtain another head. The coin flip prospects for Mega Skarmory ex are more feasible, and quite frankly, more formidable. Bewear is undoubtedly the most forgettable Pokémon ex from this set.

Dual Fusion is the best set to drop in Pokémon TCG Pocket in a long time! The cards are powerful, there are memorable Pokémon, and the artwork is stunning. What more could one ask for from a new set?! These ex cards are about to shake the meta to its core.

Happy collecting and battling!

Machop Max Monday takes place on Monday, November 2nd, 2026, from 6:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. local time, when Machop will be appearing in Power Spots. This Max Monday is the first November Max Pokémon, and it is the return of Dynamax Machop! Dynamax Machop may also appear in Max Battles through November 8th, 2026.

Dynamax Machop is a Fighting type, which means it is weak to Flying, Psychic and Fairy moves. It is a Tier 2 Dynamax Battle and costs 400 Max Particles (MP) to battle, which are only consumed if you win. Dynamax Machop can be soloed, and its Shiny form is available.

Max Monday Bonuses

  • 1 Rare Candy XL for completing in-person Max Battles
  • Power Spots will refresh more frequently
  • Additional Power Spots will be active on Mondays
Regular Sprite Shiny Sprite
Machop Machop

Want more tips and tricks for Max Battles? Read this guide.

Dynamax Machop Counters

Recommended Team

  • Vespiquen Dynamax Bug Bite /Fury Cutter /Poison Sting
  • Blissey Dynamax Pound
  • Alakazam Dynamax Max Mindstorm
  • Vespiquen is your best option as a defender for Machop. Backed up by Blissey as a healer this will work very well.
  • Alakazam is the clear best attacker for Machop.

Best Attackers for Dynamax Machop

The best attackers for defeating Dynamax Machop are the following Pokémon:

  • Alakazam Dynamax Max Mindstorm
  • Azelf Dynamax Max Mindstorm
  • Latios Dynamax Max Mindstorm
  • Espeon Dynamax Max Mindstorm
  • Metagross Dynamax Max Mindstorm
  • Moltres Dynamax Max Airstream

Best Defenders for Dynamax Machop

The best defenders to use against a Dynamax Machop are the following Pokémon:

  • Vespiquen Dynamax Bug Bite /Fury Cutter /Poison Sting
  • Gengar Dynamax Sucker Punch /Shadow Claw /Lick*
  • Hatterene Dynamax Psycho Cut
  • Latias Dynamax Dragon Breath
  • Latios Dynamax Dragon Breath
  • Butterfree Dynamax Bug Bite*

*denotes an elite TM is required.

Best Healers for Dynamax Machop

The best healers to use in a Dynamax Machop Max Battle are the following Pokémon:

  • Blissey Dynamax
  • Wailord Dynamax
  • Gigantamax Snorlax
  • Gigantamax Lapras
  • Vaporeon Dynamax
  • Eternatus

Team Composition

Dynamax Battles can be participated in by up to 4 Trainers. In each group of 4 we recommend two Trainers have teams focused on attackers, one tank/defender team, and one healer team.

Your team of 3 Pokémon should begin with a Charger, a Pokémon with a 0.5s fast move, and then two optimal attacker Pokémon.

Your Charger Pokémon should come from this list of Pokémon with 0.5s fast moves. The quicker your fast move, the quicker you can charge to the Dynamax phase. When you Dynamax, swap to your attacker, then swap back.

Remember, your Fast Move determines your attack typing in your Dynamax Phase, which is why we haven’t included any recommended Charged Moves.

Dynamax Machop Movepool

Fast Moves Charge Moves
  • Karate Chop Fighting
  • Rock Smash Fighting
  • Low Kick Fighting
  • Brick Break Fighting
  • Cross Chop Fighting
  • Low Sweep Fighting

Bosses use 2 charged moves from their movepool, which can include legacy moves:

  • One attack will damage all Pokémon currently active in battle and cannot be dodged.
  • The other is as a more powerful attack that targets only one of the active Pokémon.

The single-target move deals double the regular damage, but it can be dodged by swiping when you get the warning above your Pokémon. They do not use any of their Fast Moves.

Frequently Asked Questions

How Dynamax Battles work

To participate in a Dynamax Battles you either have to:

  • be there in-person, at Power Spots, which are easily identified on the map by the purple marking and large ‘X’ above them,
  • or join Remotely.

You can take on Dynamax Battles with up to 4 people.

  • Each person can bring up to three Pokémon in their team
  • Only Pokémon that can Dynamax or Gigantamax can participate in Max Battles
  • Max Battles are turn based, differing from both raiding and GO Battle League. 

How to charge up your Max Meter?

In a Dynamax Battle, tap the screen to use Fast Attacks as fast as possible, and ti fill up the Max Meter at the top of the screen. Your Max Meter is filled depending on how much damage you do, but never less than 1 Max Energy.

Since Dynamax Bosses have incredibly high stats, it is not worth using Charge Moves – you are better off using Fast Moves.

How to dodge Boss Attacks

When three lines appear above a Pokemon’s head, it means it is being targeted by the Max Battle Boss. You can avoid this by swiping to either the left or the right.

The Dynamax Phase

When your Max Meter reaches its maximum, your Pokémon will automatically Dynamax/Gigantamax. You can fill it up by swiping towards the energy icons that appears from time to time, or by using your Fast and Charged Attacks. Once it is full, your Pokémon will Dynamax for 3 turns.

  • You have a 3 second countdown to choose the Pokémon you wish to Dynamax / Gigantamax. You can pick any Pokémon, but it depends on which role you are fulfilling in your group. 
  • Once your Dynamax Phase ends you can immediately switch back to another Pokémon in your team if you wish to.
  • You can Dynamax more than once in a Max Battle, and will automatically Dynamax once your Max Meter refills.

If all of your Pokémon faint while battling a 3-star or higher level Boss with other Trainers, you can still help your allies by cheering for your them so that their meters fill faster.

Best Group Composition for Dynamax Battles

For Dynamax battles a maximum of 4 Trainers can enter the battle together. Generally, the best strategy for each group of 4 is to have :

  • 2 attackers
  • 1 defender
  • 1 healer

This will allow your group to stay alive as long as possible, whilst also directing damage towards one specific trainer, and allowing maximum damage to take place.

It is advisable to keep in mind that Trainers are grouped together in the order of joining the lobby, so it may be worth planning to ensure that the most prepared Trainers with levelled up Max Spirit and Max Guard are paired with others who are only prepared for attacks.

It is also worth communicating with your fellow Trainers to ensure that those who may be less prepared, such as children who don’t have the resources of others, are included in groups that can help carry them through.

Max Guard

Max Guard can be used to add a maximum of 3 shields to your Pokémon. How much HP a single shield can absorb depends on the Max Guard level.

  • 20HP for level 1
  • 40HP for level 2
  • 60 HP for level 3

When stacked to a maximum of 3 shields it gives you:

  • 60HP for level 1
  • 120HP for level 2
  • 180HP for level 3

If you find you are re-entering your Dynamax Phase and you still have shields left, it would be recommended to top back up to 3 shields, then use your Max Attack for your other moves.

While shields are only applied to the Pokémon using them, it is a hugely important aspect of a Max Battle. Whilst shielded, the Max Battle boss will direct its focused attacks towards the Pokémon that is shielded only!

The defender therefore draws damage away from the other active Pokémon in battle, protecting them from the more powerful Max Battle attack. Dodging should still be attempted in order to reduce the damage received and keep your shields up for longer. We cannot under-estimate how important Max Guard is due to it drawing damage away for your whole group, it is absolutely key to utilise in your strategy.

Only one person in your group of four needs to use Max Guard, so communication is key here.

Max Spirit

Max Spirit heals not only Pokémon using it, but also any other active Pokémon on the battle field in your group of 4. The amount of health restored is based on the level of Max Spirit and the user’s maximum HP. Aim to level up your Max Spirit to at least level 2 for a dedicated healer.

This means that Pokémon with high stamina and HP stats are better healers, even if they don’t have optimal attacks for their Max Battle boss.

Attackers in Max Battles

Attackers are Pokémon that have Max Attack levelled up. Attackers in Max Battles are the Pokémon you want to use during the Dynamax Phase. These Pokémon deal maximum damage to the Max Boss.

Remember, in Max Battles your Fast Move that determines the typing of your Max Move, so it is key to ensure it has the correct typing that will deal super effective damage to the boss. Attackers are recommended based on their typings, and their attack stats.

Defenders in Max Battles

Defenders are Pokémon that have Max Guard levelled up. Good defenders are Pokémon who have large defense and stamina stats, and take reduced damage from the Max Boss. This enables you to stay alive longer, and charge up your Max Meter faster.

Defenders are recommended based on having high level defense and stamina stats, along with their typing being resistant to the Max Bosses potential moveset.

Healers in Max Battles

Healers are Pokémon that have Max Spirit levelled up. Healers are used in the max phase to apply healing to your team. Healers are recommended based on their stamina stat. Other elements are considered, including their ability to pull double duty as defenders or attackers.

The event closes out the Twilight Trails Season with increased Shiny chances for Staryu and Elgyem, themed wild encounters and raids, rotating Field Research rewards, and a special GO Pass featuring Lucky Trade bonuses and extra Stardust.

We are currently in the Twilight Trails Season. Different days of the week will include a Daily Discovery experience. These will be active between 12:00 a.m. and 11:59 p.m. local time unless otherwise stated.

  • Additional Power Spots will be active on Mondays compared to the rest of the week.

(*) Max Battles will be available between 6:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m. local time. Power Spot availability will be limited outside of Max Mondays and Max Battle Days.

Pokémon GO’s Halloween 2026 Part Two event runs from Sunday, November 1, at 10:00 a.m. to Thursday, November 5, 2026, at 8:00 p.m. local time. Shiny Greavard makes its Pokémon GO debut, and Mega Sableye can reach the new Super Max Mega Level for the first time.

Look for Halloween-themed wild encounters, costumed Pokémon in raids, new Field Research tasks, and free Timed Research rewards. The GO Pass: Halloween 2026 continues from Part One, with Candy and Stardust bonuses available as you reach higher ranks. Here are all the event details, including research rewards and the complete GO Pass reward table.

Dates and Bonuses

Halloween 2026: Part Two Event Bonuses

The event features the following bonuses and debuts. The Candy and Stardust bonuses must be unlocked by reaching the listed GO Pass ranks.

  • 2× Candy for catching Pokémon after reaching Rank 10 on GO Pass: Halloween 2026 (3× with GO Pass Deluxe).
  • 2× Stardust for catching Pokémon after reaching Rank 20 on GO Pass: Halloween 2026 (3× with GO Pass Deluxe).
  • A remix of the Lavender Town music will be playing nightly during this year’s Halloween event. Turn up your in-game sound to feel like you’re taking a stroll through Lavender Town!

  • Mega Sableye can now reach Super Max Mega Level by using Sableye Mega Energy after reaching Max Level.

item.content:encoded:
Mega Chandelure will debut during a special Super Mega Raid Day event on Saturday, October 31, 2026, from 2:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. local time.

You can look forward to Mega Chandelure in Super Mega Raids, with the potential to be shiny (with boosted odds of 1 in 10 encounters), and up to five additional free raid passes for the day. Read on for all details, CP ranges, and everything else you need to know to prepare! Prep your best counter with our dedicated raid guide.

Featured Pokémon

Mega Chandelure

Mega Chandelure will debut in Super Mega Raids during the event! Mega Chandelure is a Ghost and Fire type Pokémon.

Chandelure can be encounter in the following CP ranges from Raid Encounters:

  • From 1784 CP to 1867 CP, with no weather boost
  • From 2231 CP to 2335 CP with Fog and Sunny weather boost

Regular and Shiny Comparison

Regular Sprite Shiny Sprite
Mega Chandelure Mega Chandelure

Bonuses

  • Increased chance to encounter shiny Chandelure from a Super Mega Raid.
  • Up to five additional free Raid Passes from spinning Gym Photo Discs (for a total of six).
  • Remote Raid limit increased to 20 from Friday,October 30, at 5:00 p.m. to Saturday, October 31,2026, at 8:00 p.m. PDT.
  • Chandelure caught from Super Mega Raids will have Mega Level 1 unlocked.

Event Ticket Bonuses

For US$4.99 (or the equivalent pricing tier in your local currency), you can purchase the event ticket offering the following bonuses:

  • Eight additional Raid Passes from spinning Gym Photo Discs (for a daily total of 14)
  • Increased chance to get Rare Candy XL from Super Mega Raid Battles
  • 5000 XP extra from all Raid Battles.
  • 5000 Stardust extra from all Raid Battles.

These bonuses will be effective on Saturday, October 31,2026, from 2:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. local time.

New Mega Level

Now you’ll be able to increase Mega Chandelure’s Mega Level all the way up to Super Max Level for the first time in Pokémon GO. As discovered during Mega Finale, Pokémon that are eligible to unlock Super Max level can learn an additional Charged Attack while they’re Mega Evolved.

Ominous Wind+

Chandelure will now be able to use an additional Charged Attack, Ominous Wind+, when it’s Mega Evolved:

  • Trainer Battles: 50 power, with a chance of increasing the user’s Attack and Defense by one stage.
  • Gyms and Raids: 145 power

The power of this attack will increase with the Pokémon’s Mega Level. You must increase a Pokémon’s Mega Level to the third level, Max, before you can increase it to Super Max.

Participate in Mega Raids to help your Pokémon reach Super Max Level as Mega Evolving alone won’t be enough, you’ll need to use that Pokémon’s Mega Energy to power it up.

Global Challenge

Get ready to take on a Global Challenge in celebration of the Chandelure Super Mega Raid Day event. Work with Trainers around the world to unlock as many tiers of the Global Challenge as possible by completing Raid Battles. The more tiers completed, the greater the bonus reward will be for Mega Chandelure!

The challenge will be active from Friday, October 30, at5:00 p.m. PDT to Saturday, October 31, 2026, at 8:00 p.m. PDT.

Based on the results of the Global Challenge, Mega Chandelure will receive the following bonuses from Monday, November 2, at 12:00 p.m. PST until Sunday, November 15, at 12:00 p.m. PST.:

  • For Mega Chandelure at the first Mega Level or higher, Ominous Wind+ will have its base power boosted*
  • Mega Chandelure at Super Max Level will have its CP boosted**

*Bonus does not apply in the GO Battle League.

**The boost is based on the number of Global Challenge tiers that have been completed.

Where to Find Super Mega Raids

Super Mega Raids will take great teamwork and may only appear at certain Gyms, so to make it easier to find nearby Gyms, Power Spots, and more, Pokémon GO has a new web-based map.

You can visit pokemongo.com/map to see the locations where Super Mega Raids might appear during an event, in addition to those in progress. You can also filter the map to show nearby community meetups days in advance. Typically, Super Mega Raids appear more likely to appear in parks and other similar locations.
